entries1.title: Israel election: Authorities dispute Netanyahu’s fraud claims
entries1.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud claims large-scale foreign involvement in the elections led by Qatar and Turkey, with Israel’s authorities so far refuting the claims.

entries1.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
entries1.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

entries1.title: China leaders demand more loyalty and more initiative
entries1.summary: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline — as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and China's economy cools down.

entries1.title: Germany seeks new head of state
entries1.summary: Who should become Germany's new president? That question is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

entries1.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
entries1.summary: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home.

entries1.title: Can EU and India work together to secure Indo-Pacific?
entries1.summary: India and Europe are deepening defense ties, but their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.

entries1.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
entries1.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

entries1.title: Shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act if the US pulls back?
entries1.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

entries1.title: Ukraine: 14 killed in Russian drone strike on crowded Dnipro train station
entries1.summary: A jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at a civilian station in Dnipro, killing and injuring passengers who were waiting to board a train. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called the attack "horrific."

entries1.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
entries1.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

entries1.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
entries1.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

entries1.title: Ship reported on fire off Oman as Iran escalation fears mount
entries1.summary: A ship in the Strait of Hormuz is reported to be on fire, a British maritime agency says. Iran has meanwhile said it has shot down another US drone as military tensions with Washington continue.

entries1.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
entries1.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

entries1.title: India news: 'Cockroaches' back Gandhi's rally against election chief
entries1.summary: The CJP said it would lend its support to any organization fighting for free and fair elections in India, including the opposition alliance. Also, India's right-wing RSS has a group of well wishers in the US. Follow DW.

entries1.title: Spain train crash: PM Sanchez calls for investigation as 3 days of mourning begins
entries1.summary: Emergency crews worked through the night after a high-speed train collision killed 69 people. PM Pedro Sanchez has pledged a full investigation into Spain's second major train accident this year.

entries1.title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc holds lead with nearly 90% of votes counted
entries1.summary: With nearly 90% of votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc is just ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, but neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.

entries1.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles into sea
entries1.summary: The latest ballistic missile launch comes amid rising border tensions with South Korea and uncertainty over potential nuclear talks with the US.

entries1.title: US: Department of Homeland Security data leak exposes details of more than 40,000 employees
entries1.summary: The leaked information reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of personnel across several US security agencies. This follows recent data breaches involving the FBI and the Defense Department.

entries1.title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
entries1.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wanted to give Canada a special status within the EU. But Germany and other member states have raised objections ahead of a summit in Montreal.

entries1.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
entries1.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of his country despite losing the presidential election runoff on Sunday. He and his family have fled to the US.

entries1.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
entries1.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

entries1.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
entries1.summary: Young people in Germany will take to the streets this weekend to demand education and action on climate change. Politicians warn that the protests could become violent, as in France, but the situations are different.

entries1.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
entries1.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

entries1.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
entries1.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

entries1.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
entries1.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

entries1.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
entries1.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

entries1.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
entries1.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

entries1.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
entries1.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

entries1.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
entries1.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

entries1.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
entries1.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

entries1.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
entries1.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

entries1.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
entries1.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

entries1.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
entries1.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

entries1.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
entries1.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

entries1.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
entries1.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

entries1.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
entries1.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

entries1.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
entries1.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

entries1.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
entries1.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

entries1.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
entries1.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

entries1.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
entries1.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

entries1.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
entries1.summary: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

entries1.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
entries1.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

entries1.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
entries1.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

entries1.title: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
entries1.summary: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.

entries1.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
entries1.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

entries1.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
entries1.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

entries1.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
entries1.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

entries1.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
entries1.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

entries1.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
entries1.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

entries1.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
entries1.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

entries1.title: Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
entries1.summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

entries1.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
entries1.summary: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

entries1.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
entries1.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

entries1.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
entries1.summary: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

entries1.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
entries1.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

entries1.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
entries1.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

entries1.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
entries1.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

entries1.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
entries1.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

entries1.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
entries1.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

entries1.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
entries1.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

entries1.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
entries1.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

entries1.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
entries1.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

entries1.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
entries1.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

entries1.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
entries1.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

entries1.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
entries1.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

entries1.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
entries1.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

entries1.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
entries1.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

entries1.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
entries1.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

entries1.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
entries1.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

entries1.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
entries1.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

entries1.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
entries1.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

entries1.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
entries1.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

entries1.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
entries1.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

entries1.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
entries1.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

entries1.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
entries1.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

entries1.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
entries1.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

entries1.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
entries1.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

entries1.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
entries1.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

entries1.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
entries1.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

entries1.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
entries1.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

entries1.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
entries1.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

entries1.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
entries1.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

entries1.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
entries1.summary: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

entries1.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
entries1.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

entries1.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
entries1.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

entries1.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
entries1.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

entries1.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
entries1.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

entries1.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
entries1.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

entries1.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
entries1.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

entries1.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
entries1.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

entries1.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
entries1.summary: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

entries1.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
entries1.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

entries1.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
entries1.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

entries1.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
entries1.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

entries1.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
entries1.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

entries1.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
entries1.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

entries1.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
entries1.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

entries1.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
entries1.summary: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

entries1.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
entries1.summary: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

entries1.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
entries1.summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

entries1.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
entries1.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

entries1.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
entries1.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

entries1.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
entries1.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

entries1.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
entries1.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

entries1.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
entries1.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

entries1.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
entries1.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

entries1.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
entries1.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

entries1.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
entries1.summary: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

entries1.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
entries1.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

entries1.title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
entries1.summary: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?

entries1.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
entries1.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

entries1.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
entries1.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

entries1.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
entries1.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

entries1.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
entries1.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

entries1.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
entries1.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

entries1.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
entries1.summary: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.

entries1.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
entries1.summary: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?

entries1.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
entries1.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City has become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

entries1.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
entries1.summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

entries1.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
entries1.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

entries1.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
entries1.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

entries1.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
entries1.summary: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

entries1.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
entries1.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

entries1.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
entries1.summary: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

entries1.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
entries1.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

entries1.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
entries1.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

entries2.title: Israel election: Authorities dispute Netanyahu’s fraud claims
entries2.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud claims large-scale foreign involvement in the elections led by Qatar and Turkey, with Israel’s authorities so far refuting the claims.

entries2.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
entries2.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

entries2.title: China leaders demand more loyalty and more initiative
entries2.summary: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline — as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and China's economy cools down.

entries2.title: Germany seeks new head of state
entries2.summary: Who should become Germany's new president? That question is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

entries2.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
entries2.summary: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home.

entries2.title: Can EU and India work together to secure Indo-Pacific?
entries2.summary: India and Europe are deepening defense ties, but their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.

entries2.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
entries2.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

entries2.title: Shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act if the US pulls back?
entries2.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

entries2.title: Ukraine: 14 killed in Russian drone strike on crowded Dnipro train station
entries2.summary: A jet-powered drone struck a crowded platform at a civilian station in Dnipro, killing and injuring passengers who were waiting to board a train. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called the attack "horrific."

entries2.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
entries2.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

entries2.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
entries2.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

entries2.title: Ship reported on fire off Oman as Iran escalation fears mount
entries2.summary: A ship in the Strait of Hormuz is reported to be on fire, a British maritime agency says. Iran has meanwhile said it has shot down another US drone as military tensions with Washington continue.

entries2.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
entries2.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

entries2.title: India news: 'Cockroaches' back Gandhi's rally against election chief
entries2.summary: The CJP said it would lend its support to any organization fighting for free and fair elections in India, including the opposition alliance. Also, India's right-wing RSS has a group of well wishers in the US. Follow DW.

entries2.title: Spain train crash: PM Sanchez calls for investigation as 3 days of mourning begins
entries2.summary: Emergency crews worked through the night after a high-speed train collision killed 69 people. PM Pedro Sanchez has pledged a full investigation into Spain's second major train accident this year.

entries2.title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc holds lead with nearly 90% of votes counted
entries2.summary: With nearly 90% of votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc is just ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, but neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.

entries2.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles into sea
entries2.summary: The latest ballistic missile launch comes amid rising border tensions with South Korea and uncertainty over potential nuclear talks with the US.

entries2.title: US: Department of Homeland Security data leak exposes details of more than 40,000 employees
entries2.summary: The leaked information reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of personnel across several US security agencies. This follows recent data breaches involving the FBI and the Defense Department.

entries2.title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
entries2.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wanted to give Canada a special status within the EU. But Germany and other member states have raised objections ahead of a summit in Montreal.

entries2.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in US, declares himself 'leader' of Brazil
entries2.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself the rightful leader of his country despite losing the presidential election runoff on Sunday. He and his family have fled to the US.

entries2.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
entries2.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

entries2.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
entries2.summary: Young people in Germany will take to the streets this weekend to demand education and action on climate change. Politicians warn that the protests could become violent, as in France, but the situations are different.

entries2.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
entries2.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

entries2.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
entries2.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

entries2.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
entries2.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

entries2.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
entries2.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

entries2.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
entries2.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

entries2.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
entries2.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

entries2.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
entries2.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

entries2.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
entries2.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

entries2.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
entries2.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

entries2.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
entries2.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

entries2.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
entries2.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

entries2.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
entries2.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

entries2.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
entries2.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

entries2.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
entries2.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

entries2.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
entries2.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

entries2.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
entries2.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

entries2.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
entries2.summary: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

entries2.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
entries2.summary: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

entries2.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
entries2.summary: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

entries2.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
entries2.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

entries2.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
entries2.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

entries2.title: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
entries2.summary: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.

entries2.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
entries2.summary: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

entries2.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
entries2.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

entries2.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
entries2.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

entries2.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
entries2.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

entries2.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
entries2.summary: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

entries2.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
entries2.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

entries2.title: Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
entries2.summary: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

entries2.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
entries2.summary: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

entries2.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
entries2.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

entries2.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
entries2.summary: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

entries2.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
entries2.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

entries2.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
entries2.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

entries2.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
entries2.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

entries2.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
entries2.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

entries2.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
entries2.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

entries2.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
entries2.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

entries2.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
entries2.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

entries2.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
entries2.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

entries2.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
entries2.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

entries2.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
entries2.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

entries2.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
entries2.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

entries2.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
entries2.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

entries2.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
entries2.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

entries2.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
entries2.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

entries2.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
entries2.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

entries2.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
entries2.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

entries2.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
entries2.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

entries2.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
entries2.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

entries2.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
entries2.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

entries2.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
entries2.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

entries2.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
entries2.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

entries2.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
entries2.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

entries2.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
entries2.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

entries2.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
entries2.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

entries2.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
entries2.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

entries2.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
entries2.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

entries2.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
entries2.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

entries2.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
entries2.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

entries2.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
entries2.summary: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

entries2.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
entries2.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

entries2.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
entries2.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

entries2.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
entries2.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

entries2.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
entries2.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

entries2.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
entries2.summary: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

entries2.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
entries2.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

entries2.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
entries2.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

entries2.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
entries2.summary: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

entries2.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
entries2.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

entries2.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
entries2.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

entries2.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
entries2.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

entries2.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
entries2.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

entries2.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
entries2.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

entries2.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
entries2.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

entries2.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
entries2.summary: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

entries2.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
entries2.summary: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

entries2.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
entries2.summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

entries2.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
entries2.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

entries2.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
entries2.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

entries2.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
entries2.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

entries2.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
entries2.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

entries2.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
entries2.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

entries2.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
entries2.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

entries2.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
entries2.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

entries2.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
entries2.summary: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

entries2.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
entries2.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

entries2.title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
entries2.summary: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?

entries2.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
entries2.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

entries2.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
entries2.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

entries2.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
entries2.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

entries2.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
entries2.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

entries2.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
entries2.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

entries2.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
entries2.summary: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.

entries2.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
entries2.summary: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?

entries2.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
entries2.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City has become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

entries2.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
entries2.summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

entries2.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
entries2.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

entries2.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
entries2.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

entries2.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
entries2.summary: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

entries2.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
entries2.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

entries2.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
entries2.summary: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

entries2.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
entries2.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

entries2.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
entries2.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.
