entries1.title: 'An absurdity' to blame human error: Spain's deadly train crash 'should never' have happened
entries1.summary: Following Spain's deadly high-speed train crash, Delano D'Souza is joined by Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, Railway Structural & PRM Certification Expert. Batea challenges explanations that reduce railway disasters to isolated human mistakes. “It is basically an absurdity to say that it depended on one person and one human mistake,” he argues, emphasizing that modern railway networks operate through multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train-detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight. “The system has been designed in a way that this type of accident should never happen.”

entries1.title: DR Congo: A centre celebrates the discharge of last Ebola patients
entries1.summary: Medical staff and residents at a treatment centre in Ituri danced and sang to celebrate a first since May: the centre is no longer treating any confirmed Ebola cases.

entries1.title: Ireland becomes refuge for anti-Trump Americans
entries1.summary: They have left everything behind to get away from US President Donald Trump's America. Entrepreneurs, academics, scientists and students: tens of thousands of US citizens have moved to Ireland in recent years. Last year alone, some 10,000 Americans settled there and nearly 100 even applied for asylum – citing political, racial or gender persecution.

entries1.title: Ian McEwan speculates on 'What We Can Know' in the 22nd century
entries1.summary: Booker Prize-winning author Ian McEwan sits down with Olivia Salazar-Winspear to discuss the 22nd century society he created in "What We Can Know", as his latest novel is translated into French. While his characters grapple with the aftermath of the great "derangement", in a world where many of the 21st century's capital cities have been submerged, we discuss our upcoming reckoning with the climate crisis.

entries1.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s great escape: Is this the beginning of the end for ‘Bolsonarism’?
entries1.summary: The Brazilian election results had barely been announced before the defeated presidential candidate, Flavio Bolsonaro, packed his bags and fled with his family to the United States. The move may have dealt a serious blow to the already tarnished family brand, but does it spell the end for “Bolsonarism”?

entries1.title: Aid mission set to enter Ukraine's Oleshky as localised ceasefire holds for third day
entries1.summary: A humanitarian aid mission is set to enter the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, a Ukrainian official said on Thuirsday, as a localised truce between Kyiv and Moscow, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, held for a third day. Some 2,000 residents in the Russian occupied city have been cut off from essential supplies amid reports that many are starving.

entries1.title: A tale of two economies: How America's cost-of-living crisis is shaping US midterm elections
entries1.summary: The economy is the number one issue for most American voters, as they worry about high food and energy costs. But can the results of November's midterm elections really impact the cost-of-living crisis? "There isn't a ton that anyone can do about it, regardless of who wins the midterms," says Greg Ip, chief economics commentator at The Wall Street Journal.

entries1.title: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visit injured in train crash at Toledo hospital
entries1.summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived at Toledo University Hospital on Thursday to visit those injured in the train accident in Urda – in which at least 69 people died – who are being treated at this hospital, 15 of whom are in the ICU. The King and Queen will meet with the medical team and subsequently visit several of the injured, who will be accompanied by their families. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from oledo University Hospital.

entries1.title: Ireland opens arms to Americans fleeing US President Donald Trump
entries1.summary: Tens of thousands of US citizens have fled the United States since Donald Trump's return to power two years ago. Given the language and a shared history, Ireland has been among the top choices for Americans looking for an alternative. FRANCE 24's team reports.

entries1.title: Pentagon shake-up continues: US fires top army general in latest ouster
entries1.summary: The United States has fired its top military planner, The Atlantic reported Wednesday, in a surprise shake-up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. His ouster would be the latest in a series of high-profile departures from the military since Trump returned to power a year ago.

entries1.title: Food safety in India: A challenge for the world's most populous country
entries1.summary: India's food industry feeds more than a billion people every day. But ensuring that what reaches consumers is safe has become an increasingly difficult challenge. The country has witnessed a rise in cases of food adulteration, with sometimes fatal consequences. As concerns over adulteration and poor hygiene grow, questions are being raised about whether regulators can effectively oversee such a sprawling sector.

entries1.title: US Midterms: Donald Trump and Barack Obama make closing pitches
entries1.summary: In the United States, Democrats are turning to Barack Obama to rally voters ahead of the midterm elections, a crucial test that could shape the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency. The former president has addressed three campaign rallies this week, with the latest one in Atlanta, Georgia. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.

entries1.title: Spain reckons with second deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
entries1.summary: Wednesday's deadly train crash has dealt a serious blow to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s campaign. The accident in Toledo province killed 69 people and came just nine months after another deadly crash on the same line, leading to accusations from experts and the public of underinvestment in railway infrastructure under Sanchez's government after years of rapid network ​expansion.

entries1.title: Trump and Obama trade barbs in closing week of US midterm election
entries1.summary: Neither man is on the ​ballot but Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington. Thirty-five ‌of the 100 Senate seats and all 435 seats in the House of Representatives are being contested next Tuesday. Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats' chances of capturing a majority in the ⁠House, with the contest for the Senate seen as very close.

entries1.title: Minimum wage increase could come early as France braces for protests
entries1.summary: The French government is looking for new ways to calm social unrest ahead of more planned demonstrations over the cost of living this weekend. The minimum wage was set to increase on January 1, 2027. Now, officials are considering making the change one month earlier and adding an extra boost.

entries1.title: 'Real questions to be asked' after deadly train collision in Spain, journalist says
entries1.summary: In this edition of Perspective, we focus on the tragic train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday. We're joined by Nicholas Kingsley, executive editor of Railway Gazette International.

entries1.title: Why is Donald Trump avoiding the Epstein case at all costs?
entries1.summary: The midterm elections campaign is in full swing in the United States, but Donald Trump is doing his utmost to avoid one subject: the Epstein Files. On January 30, the US Department of Justice published the court records relating to the Epstein case. At FRANCE 24, two of our journalists, Samia Metheni and Ava Luquet, delve into the 3 million documents to understand how Epstein's network operated. What did they find looking through the documents and what impact do they still have on Trump? Ava Luquet answered François Picard's questions.

entries1.title: Paris becomes an open-air museum
entries1.summary: In this edition of Entre Nous, we meet David-Hervé Boutin, curator at "L'art dans la ville". He explores how the Getty Museum is bringing its collection to the streets of Paris. Masterpieces will be displayed on six of the city's façades, offering a unique open-air art experience throughout the French capital.

entries1.title: Putin seeks to expand ties with African countries at Russia-Africa summit
entries1.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday hosted dozens of African leaders at a Russia-Africa summit, part of Moscow’s efforts to expand its influence across the continent. The Russia-Africa summit marks a renewed Kremlin effort to bolster ties with a continent of nearly 1.6 billion people that is increasingly assertive on the global stage.

entries1.title: DRC: C64 opposition coalition meets in Rome, calls for inclusive dialogue
entries1.summary: Democratic Republic ⁠of Congo's main ​opposition coalition, C64, met in Rome on Tuesday. Under pressure to respond to Joseph Kabila’s rebellion, its five leaders addressed the situation in the country from the Italian capital. They condemned any seizure of power by force and called for inclusive dialogue. FRANCE 24’s Emmet Livingston reports.

entries1.title: France: Trappes racist shooting suspect transferred to French court
entries1.summary: French anti-terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen said the suspect in the Trappes racist attack, which killed one person and injured five others, had been brought before a French court. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.

entries1.title: Niger: Guards accused of 'cruel, inhuman' treatment after 33 die in detention
entries1.summary: In Niger, guards ignored the panicked cries for help from 33 detainees who died in a detention cell last month. Reports indicate that 72 people were crowded into a poorly ventilated, 20-square-metre space, where dozens slowly suffocated over 11 hours. The cell may have been cleaned and disinfected before it could be investigated. FRANCE 24's correspondent Sam Olukoya has more.

entries1.title: 'Very disturbing details': Trappes shooting suspect admits targeting victims by race, religion
entries1.summary: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to "targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African," prosecutors said on Thursday. FRANCE 24's Charli James reports.

entries1.title: Spain begins three days of mourning after train crash kills 69
entries1.summary: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, in which one train struck another from behind, killing 69 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network ahead of a national election. Three days of mourning have begun in the country.

entries2.title: 'An absurdity' to blame human error: Spain's deadly train crash 'should never' have happened
entries2.summary: Following Spain's deadly high-speed train crash, Delano D'Souza is joined by Francisco Badea, Director of FEM Expert Engineering, Railway Structural & PRM Certification Expert. Batea challenges explanations that reduce railway disasters to isolated human mistakes. “It is basically an absurdity to say that it depended on one person and one human mistake,” he argues, emphasizing that modern railway networks operate through multiple layers of protection, including automated safeguards, train-detection technologies, operational protocols and institutional oversight. “The system has been designed in a way that this type of accident should never happen.”

entries2.title: DR Congo: A centre celebrates the discharge of last Ebola patients
entries2.summary: Medical staff and residents at a treatment centre in Ituri danced and sang to celebrate a first since May: the centre is no longer treating any confirmed Ebola cases.

entries2.title: Ireland becomes refuge for anti-Trump Americans
entries2.summary: They have left everything behind to get away from US President Donald Trump's America. Entrepreneurs, academics, scientists and students: tens of thousands of US citizens have moved to Ireland in recent years. Last year alone, some 10,000 Americans settled there and nearly 100 even applied for asylum – citing political, racial or gender persecution.

entries2.title: Ian McEwan speculates on 'What We Can Know' in the 22nd century
entries2.summary: Booker Prize-winning author Ian McEwan sits down with Olivia Salazar-Winspear to discuss the 22nd century society he created in "What We Can Know", as his latest novel is translated into French. While his characters grapple with the aftermath of the great "derangement", in a world where many of the 21st century's capital cities have been submerged, we discuss our upcoming reckoning with the climate crisis.

entries2.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s great escape: Is this the beginning of the end for ‘Bolsonarism’?
entries2.summary: The Brazilian election results had barely been announced before the defeated presidential candidate, Flavio Bolsonaro, packed his bags and fled with his family to the United States. The move may have dealt a serious blow to the already tarnished family brand, but does it spell the end for “Bolsonarism”?

entries2.title: Aid mission set to enter Ukraine's Oleshky as localised ceasefire holds for third day
entries2.summary: A humanitarian aid mission is set to enter the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, a Ukrainian official said on Thuirsday, as a localised truce between Kyiv and Moscow, brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, held for a third day. Some 2,000 residents in the Russian occupied city have been cut off from essential supplies amid reports that many are starving.

entries2.title: A tale of two economies: How America's cost-of-living crisis is shaping US midterm elections
entries2.summary: The economy is the number one issue for most American voters, as they worry about high food and energy costs. But can the results of November's midterm elections really impact the cost-of-living crisis? "There isn't a ton that anyone can do about it, regardless of who wins the midterms," says Greg Ip, chief economics commentator at The Wall Street Journal.

entries2.title: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visit injured in train crash at Toledo hospital
entries2.summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia arrived at Toledo University Hospital on Thursday to visit those injured in the train accident in Urda – in which at least 69 people died – who are being treated at this hospital, 15 of whom are in the ICU. The King and Queen will meet with the medical team and subsequently visit several of the injured, who will be accompanied by their families. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from oledo University Hospital.

entries2.title: Ireland opens arms to Americans fleeing US President Donald Trump
entries2.summary: Tens of thousands of US citizens have fled the United States since Donald Trump's return to power two years ago. Given the language and a shared history, Ireland has been among the top choices for Americans looking for an alternative. FRANCE 24's team reports.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1f220fdc-d3a7-11f1-940f-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-50d6a632.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1f220fdc-d3a7-11f1-940f-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-50d6a632.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">080c43f0-d3a5-11f1-85cb-893570fa81c2</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:31:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Pentagon shake-up continues: US fires top army general in latest ouster</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-pentagon-shake-up-continues-us-fires-top-army-general-in-latest-ouster</link><description>
The United States has fired its top military planner, The Atlantic reported Wednesday, in a surprise shake-up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. His ouster would be the latest in a series of high-profile departures from the military since Trump returned to power a year ago.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9629dd76-d3ac-11f1-900b-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-160839-161020-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9629dd76-d3ac-11f1-900b-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-160839-161020-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9bc78774-d3ac-11f1-82ee-afb5a3a6156b</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:30:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>Food safety in India: A challenge for the world's most populous country</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20261029-food-safety-in-india-a-challenge-for-the-world-s-most-populous-country</link><description>
India's food industry feeds more than a billion people every day. But ensuring that what reaches consumers is safe has become an increasingly difficult challenge. The country has witnessed a rise in cases of food adulteration, with sometimes fatal consequences. As concerns over adulteration and poor hygiene grow, questions are being raised about whether regulators can effectively oversee such a sprawling sector.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3c02c5bc-d39b-11f1-a686-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bf7600e4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3c02c5bc-d39b-11f1-a686-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bf7600e4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2a525e18-d2e7-11f1-87df-79b15ca8b9e2</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:15:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Selma DAOUI</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US Midterms: Donald Trump and Barack Obama make closing pitches</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-us-midterms-donald-trump-and-barack-obama-make-closing-pitches</link><description>
In the United States, Democrats are turning to Barack Obama to rally voters ahead of the midterm elections, a crucial test that could shape the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency. The former president has addressed three campaign rallies this week, with the latest one in Atlanta, Georgia. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1f9cf956-d396-11f1-bc3c-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-131556-132110-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1f9cf956-d396-11f1-bc3c-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-131556-132110-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">256a4406-d396-11f1-a295-29a62a977261</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:57:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Spain reckons with second deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-spain-reckons-with-second-deadly-train-crash-of-the-year-ahead-of-national-election</link><description>
Wednesday's deadly train crash has dealt a serious blow to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s campaign. The accident in Toledo province killed 69 people and came just nine months after another deadly crash on the same line, leading to accusations from experts and the public of underinvestment in railway infrastructure under Sanchez's government after years of rapid network ​expansion.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e1d1f28e-d3a4-11f1-8926-27b8c5a16f5e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-143126-143322-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e1d1f28e-d3a4-11f1-8926-27b8c5a16f5e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-143126-143322-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e6ded0bc-d3a4-11f1-a498-893570fa81c2</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:50:53 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Trump and Obama trade barbs in closing week of US midterm election</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-trump-and-obama-trade-barbs-in-closing-week-of-us-midterm-election</link><description>
Neither man is on the ​ballot but Republican President Donald Trump and Democratic former President Barack Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington. Thirty-five ‌of the 100 Senate seats and all 435 seats in the House of Representatives are being contested next Tuesday. Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats' chances of capturing a majority in the ⁠House, with the contest for the Senate seen as very close.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/969f8fe6-d3a5-11f1-b6f4-27b8c5a16f5e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-143709-143855-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/969f8fe6-d3a5-11f1-b6f4-27b8c5a16f5e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-143709-143855-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9bf0f62e-d3a5-11f1-a951-392311e2abfb</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:48:42 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Minimum wage increase could come early as France braces for protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-minimum-wage-increase-could-come-early-as-france-braces-for-protests</link><description>
The French government is looking for new ways to calm social unrest ahead of more planned demonstrations over the cost of living this weekend. The minimum wage was set to increase on January 1, 2027. Now, officials are considering making the change one month earlier and adding an extra boost.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/18972928-d3a6-11f1-9ac8-cfde22befba6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-144016-144143-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/18972928-d3a6-11f1-9ac8-cfde22befba6/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-144016-144143-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1d996bc0-d3a6-11f1-8fe1-ed4739f57c7d</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:47:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'Real questions to be asked' after deadly train collision in Spain, journalist says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261029-real-questions-to-be-asked-after-deadly-train-collision-in-spain-journalist-says</link><description>
In this edition of Perspective, we focus on the tragic train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday. We're joined by Nicholas Kingsley, executive editor of Railway Gazette International. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8b42153e-d3a4-11f1-96d9-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-698c25be.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8b42153e-d3a4-11f1-96d9-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-698c25be.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a2869064-d38e-11f1-99f7-93c98f0401df</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:44:07 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Charles PELLEGRIN</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Why is Donald Trump avoiding the Epstein case at all costs?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-why-is-donald-trump-avoiding-the-epstein-case-at-all-costs</link><description>
The midterm elections campaign is in full swing in the United States, but Donald Trump is doing his utmost to avoid one subject: the Epstein Files. On January 30, the US Department of Justice published the court records relating to the Epstein case. At FRANCE 24, two of our journalists, Samia Metheni and Ava Luquet, delve into the 3 million documents to understand how Epstein's network operated. What did they find looking through the documents and what impact do they still have on Trump? Ava Luquet answered François Picard's questions.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1306183a-d3a5-11f1-acf7-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a74547dd.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1306183a-d3a5-11f1-acf7-79db0eb73735/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a74547dd.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fabf5e2c-d3a3-11f1-937f-b97f32cee220</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:37:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Entre Nous</category><title>Paris becomes an open-air museum</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/entre-nous/20261029-paris-becomes-an-open-air-museum</link><description>
In this edition of Entre Nous, we meet David-Hervé Boutin, curator at "L'art dans la ville". He explores how the Getty Museum is bringing its collection to the streets of Paris. Masterpieces will be displayed on six of the city's façades, offering a unique open-air art experience throughout the French capital.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3647bc7e-d3a3-11f1-94e8-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-ed826d4e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3647bc7e-d3a3-11f1-94e8-15e3238b6981/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-ed826d4e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">29ba3edc-d399-11f1-9450-47790bd7eff0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:23:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Delano D’SOUZA</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Putin seeks to expand ties with African countries at Russia-Africa summit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-putin-seeks-to-expand-ties-with-african-countries-at-russia-africa-summit</link><description>
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday hosted dozens of African leaders at a Russia-Africa summit, part of Moscow’s efforts to expand its influence across the continent. The Russia-Africa summit marks a renewed Kremlin effort to bolster ties with a continent of nearly 1.6 billion people that is increasingly assertive on the global stage. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0c0aa0bc-d37f-11f1-bedb-811458fcf026/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T091823Z-1533690092-RC2WCOA2IVT4-RTRMADP-3-RUSSIA-AFRICA-SUMMIT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0c0aa0bc-d37f-11f1-bedb-811458fcf026/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T091823Z-1533690092-RC2WCOA2IVT4-RTRMADP-3-RUSSIA-AFRICA-SUMMIT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f9182ffe-d37b-11f1-a580-6f50dc8232ce</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:32:56 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>DRC: C64 opposition coalition meets in Rome, calls for inclusive dialogue</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-drc-c64-opposition-coalition-meets-in-rome-calls-for-inclusive-dialogue</link><description>
Democratic Republic ⁠of Congo's main ​opposition coalition, C64, met in Rome on Tuesday. Under pressure to respond to Joseph Kabila’s rebellion, its five leaders addressed the situation in the country from the Italian capital. They condemned any seizure of power by force and called for inclusive dialogue. FRANCE 24’s Emmet Livingston reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8e046638-d380-11f1-9913-efcc5769f1db/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-aad464c0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8e046638-d380-11f1-9913-efcc5769f1db/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-aad464c0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eea3f77c-d37d-11f1-9a48-a7be7c903c4d</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:28:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France: Trappes racist shooting suspect transferred to French court</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-france-trappes-racist-shooting-suspect-transferred-to-french-court</link><description>
French anti-terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen said the suspect in the Trappes racist attack, which killed one person and injured five others, had been brought before a French court. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Philip Turle has more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f3992ac0-d069-11f1-bfa8-bba4eee3dc72/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26296487849716.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f3992ac0-d069-11f1-bfa8-bba4eee3dc72/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26296487849716.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3c6536a8-d386-11f1-a783-2d810c4dd5ee</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:22:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Niger: Guards accused of 'cruel, inhuman' treatment after 33 die in detention</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-niger-guards-accused-of-cruel-inhuman-treatment-after-33-die-in-detention</link><description>
In Niger, guards ignored the panicked cries for help from 33 detainees who died in a detention cell last month. Reports indicate that 72 people were crowded into a poorly ventilated, 20-square-metre space, where dozens slowly suffocated over 11 hours. The cell may have been cleaned and disinfected before it could be investigated. FRANCE 24's correspondent Sam Olukoya has more.
 

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/57aff1c4-d38a-11f1-9cd7-a7bbbeea0b20/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-99a1b234.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/57aff1c4-d38a-11f1-9cd7-a7bbbeea0b20/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-99a1b234.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">82b2af6a-d385-11f1-8861-bb5448debf37</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:17:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>'Very disturbing details': Trappes shooting suspect admits targeting victims by race, religion</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-very-disturbing-details-trappes-shooting-suspect-admits-targeting-victims-by-race-religion</link><description>
A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to "targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African," prosecutors said on Thursday. FRANCE 24's Charli James reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/312dc992-d38d-11f1-8e0c-75c7729144f1/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-113113-113351-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/312dc992-d38d-11f1-8e0c-75c7729144f1/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-113113-113351-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36b07694-d38d-11f1-8731-6f8f245a9f0a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:10:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Spain begins three days of mourning after train crash kills 69</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261029-spain-begins-three-days-of-mourning-after-train-crash-kills-69</link><description>
Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, in which one train struck another from behind, killing 69 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network ahead of a national election. Three days of mourning have begun in the country.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed34d77e-d38e-11f1-a53c-75c7729144f1/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-64b94184.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed34d77e-d38e-11f1-a53c-75c7729144f1/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-64b94184.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">92cad1a8-d38e-11f1-8128-4bdd9e2d2dc0</guid><pubDate>Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:01:58 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

entries1.title: Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'
entries1.summary: The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.

entries1.title: Real Madrid says Mbappé was wrong over Mao Zedong as China fallout continues
entries1.summary: Spanish football club Real Madrid, as well as Spanish league bosses, were on Thursday waiting to see if their apologies had led to a thaw in relations with China following striker Kylian Mbappé's comments about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

entries1.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
entries1.summary: A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.

entries1.title: Spain begins three days of national mourning after train crash kills at least 68
entries1.summary: Spain on Thursday began three days of official mourning, after a rail collision south of Madrid on Wednesday killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100.

entries1.title: Russia-Africa summit tests Moscow's ambitions for broader influence
entries1.summary: More than 20 African leaders are in Moscow for a summit that will test Russia's bid to expand its influence on the continent. The two-day Russia-Africa Summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy sanctions over its Ukraine offensive – and as several African governments turn to it for security assistance.

entries1.title: Medical experts warn climate change is now a 'global health emergency'
entries1.summary: The damage wreaked by climate change on human health is escalating, experts warn, with deaths from heat, drought and other extreme weather rising faster than the world is taking action to limit global warming. Published on Wednesday, a report by medical journal The Lancet calls for climate change to be declared "a global health emergency".

entries1.title: French Senate toughens proposals to make rioters pay for damage
entries1.summary: The upper house of the French parliament has toughened a proposed law that would make people who participate in rioting and vandalism liable for up to €10,000, after nationwide protests against failing schools and the cost of living that turned violent in Paris and other cities. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the democratic right to protest.

entries1.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
entries1.summary: Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.

entries1.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
entries1.summary: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.

entries1.title: French media protest manhandling of journalists at far-right party rally
entries1.summary: More than 40 French media groups, including Radio France International, have called on Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally (RN) to allow them to work freely after journalists were allegedly subjected to rough treatment at a party congress last weekend.

entries1.title: Iraqi court jails seven French nationals over Islamic State membership
entries1.summary: An Iraqi court has sentenced seven French nationals to prison for belonging to the Islamic State armed group, handing down the first verdicts in proceedings involving French detainees transferred from Syria last year.

entries1.title: Somalia reports deadly fighting with Al-Shabaab as both sides claim heavy losses
entries1.summary: Somalia’s government and Al-Shabaab militants have issued sharply conflicting accounts of deadly fighting near the southern city of Leego, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy losses during a battle on Monday.

entries1.title: PSG bosses hail club of the year success at 2026 Ballon d'Or awards
entries1.summary: Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi on Tuesday praised head coach Luis Enrique and his squad after the club retained the Ballon d’Or Club of the Year award.

entries1.title: France pledges university admissions overhaul and education funding to ease protests
entries1.summary: France’s government has promised to replace Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and to invest in schools and student support, offering a package of concessions aimed at defusing weeks of protests over education and the rising cost of living.

entries1.title: Polls open in Israel as Netanyahu faces close contest after three years of war
entries1.summary: Polls opened in Israel on Tuesday in the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a close contest after three years of war and deepening political divisions.

entries1.title: Macron vows to stand firm against disorder during visit to Marseille
entries1.summary: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday gave his full support to security forces as France prepared for a third consecutive weekend of protests over the poor state of schools and the rising cost of living.

entries1.title: Putellas and Kane win 2026 Ballon d'Or as PSG retain men's team of year prize
entries1.summary: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas and the Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 women's and men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night as Paris Saint-Germain retained the men's team of the year award.

entries1.title: Senegal PM vows to address economic issues as 2026 Youth Olympics Games loom
entries1.summary: Senegal's Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo on Monday promised to solve the battle over the budget between members of the ruling Pastef party as the country counts down for the start of the 2026 Youth Olympic games on Saturday.

entries1.title: Le Pen widens poll lead as Mélenchon closes in on run-off spot
entries1.summary: Former French prime minister Édouard Philippe would finish only third in the first round of the presidential election, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon, according to a new Cluster 17 poll for Politico published on Monday.

entries1.title: Serbia's student movement ousts longtime leader Vucic
entries1.summary: Serbia's student-led movement was on Monday enjoying its first day of power after ending the 14-year reign of Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party.

entries1.title: Macron leads congratulations to Lula over election victory in Brazil
entries1.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron was among the world leaders on Monday to hail Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's re-election as Brazil's president.

entries1.title: French unions and protest groups call fresh rallies and nationwide strike
entries1.summary: French unions and protest groups have called for fresh demonstrations on 31 October and a nationwide strike on 5 November, seeking to build on a movement over wages, living costs and public services after a massive police deployment helped contain unrest during Saturday’s marches.

entries2.title: Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'
entries2.summary: The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.

entries2.title: Real Madrid says Mbappé was wrong over Mao Zedong as China fallout continues
entries2.summary: Spanish football club Real Madrid, as well as Spanish league bosses, were on Thursday waiting to see if their apologies had led to a thaw in relations with China following striker Kylian Mbappé's comments about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

entries2.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
entries2.summary: A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.

entries2.title: Spain begins three days of national mourning after train crash kills at least 68
entries2.summary: Spain on Thursday began three days of official mourning, after a rail collision south of Madrid on Wednesday killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100.

entries2.title: Russia-Africa summit tests Moscow's ambitions for broader influence
entries2.summary: More than 20 African leaders are in Moscow for a summit that will test Russia's bid to expand its influence on the continent. The two-day Russia-Africa Summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy sanctions over its Ukraine offensive – and as several African governments turn to it for security assistance.

entries2.title: Medical experts warn climate change is now a 'global health emergency'
entries2.summary: The damage wreaked by climate change on human health is escalating, experts warn, with deaths from heat, drought and other extreme weather rising faster than the world is taking action to limit global warming. Published on Wednesday, a report by medical journal The Lancet calls for climate change to be declared "a global health emergency".

entries2.title: French Senate toughens proposals to make rioters pay for damage
entries2.summary: The upper house of the French parliament has toughened a proposed law that would make people who participate in rioting and vandalism liable for up to €10,000, after nationwide protests against failing schools and the cost of living that turned violent in Paris and other cities. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the democratic right to protest.

entries2.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
entries2.summary: Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.

entries2.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
entries2.summary: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.

entries2.title: French media protest manhandling of journalists at far-right party rally
entries2.summary: More than 40 French media groups, including Radio France International, have called on Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally (RN) to allow them to work freely after journalists were allegedly subjected to rough treatment at a party congress last weekend.

entries2.title: Iraqi court jails seven French nationals over Islamic State membership
entries2.summary: An Iraqi court has sentenced seven French nationals to prison for belonging to the Islamic State armed group, handing down the first verdicts in proceedings involving French detainees transferred from Syria last year.

entries2.title: Somalia reports deadly fighting with Al-Shabaab as both sides claim heavy losses
entries2.summary: Somalia’s government and Al-Shabaab militants have issued sharply conflicting accounts of deadly fighting near the southern city of Leego, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy losses during a battle on Monday.

entries2.title: PSG bosses hail club of the year success at 2026 Ballon d'Or awards
entries2.summary: Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi on Tuesday praised head coach Luis Enrique and his squad after the club retained the Ballon d’Or Club of the Year award.

entries2.title: France pledges university admissions overhaul and education funding to ease protests
entries2.summary: France’s government has promised to replace Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and to invest in schools and student support, offering a package of concessions aimed at defusing weeks of protests over education and the rising cost of living.

entries2.title: Polls open in Israel as Netanyahu faces close contest after three years of war
entries2.summary: Polls opened in Israel on Tuesday in the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a close contest after three years of war and deepening political divisions.

entries2.title: Macron vows to stand firm against disorder during visit to Marseille
entries2.summary: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday gave his full support to security forces as France prepared for a third consecutive weekend of protests over the poor state of schools and the rising cost of living.

entries2.title: Putellas and Kane win 2026 Ballon d'Or as PSG retain men's team of year prize
entries2.summary: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas and the Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 women's and men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night as Paris Saint-Germain retained the men's team of the year award.

entries2.title: Senegal PM vows to address economic issues as 2026 Youth Olympics Games loom
entries2.summary: Senegal's Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo on Monday promised to solve the battle over the budget between members of the ruling Pastef party as the country counts down for the start of the 2026 Youth Olympic games on Saturday.

entries2.title: Le Pen widens poll lead as Mélenchon closes in on run-off spot
entries2.summary: Former French prime minister Édouard Philippe would finish only third in the first round of the presidential election, behind Jean-Luc Mélenchon, according to a new Cluster 17 poll for Politico published on Monday.

entries2.title: Serbia's student movement ousts longtime leader Vucic
entries2.summary: Serbia's student-led movement was on Monday enjoying its first day of power after ending the 14-year reign of Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party.

entries2.title: Macron leads congratulations to Lula over election victory in Brazil
entries2.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron was among the world leaders on Monday to hail Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's re-election as Brazil's president.

entries2.title: French unions and protest groups call fresh rallies and nationwide strike
entries2.summary: French unions and protest groups have called for fresh demonstrations on 31 October and a nationwide strike on 5 November, seeking to build on a movement over wages, living costs and public services after a massive police deployment helped contain unrest during Saturday’s marches.

entries1.title: Italian military helicopter on EU peacekeeping mission crashes in Bosnia
entries1.summary: The aircraft was involved in Operation Althea. The causes of the accident still have to be established.

entries1.title: Death toll from Spain train crash rises to 74 as royals visit victims
entries1.summary: Spain's King Felipe VI expressed his sorrow over the "terrible accident" as he and Queen Letizia visited a hospital where injured victims were being treated.

entries1.title: Latest news bulletin | October 29th, 2026 – Evening
entries1.summary: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 29th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

entries1.title: Major strikes planned across Italy on Friday against cost of living and military spending
entries1.summary: Strikes and rallies are planned over rising living cost and the shift of public funds to arms. Unions are demanding wage increases in line with inflation; while dockworkers in 17 countries are mobilising against the war.

entries1.title: Deadly train crash puts Sánchez on the ropes a month before elections
entries1.summary: Wednesday's accident happened in the middle of the pre-election campaign, adding pressure to Sánchez's government. With a month to go, parties are locked in a blame battle.

entries1.title: EU countries push back against Brussels plan to tax gas more than electricity
entries1.summary: More than a dozen EU countries are challenging Brussels' plans to favour electricity over gas, warning that the proposals would undermine national control over energy taxation and grid charges.

entries1.title: German serial rapist sentenced to 12 years as police investigate 44 more cases
entries1.summary: Frank S. was sentenced to 12 years in prison, followed by preventive detention. The 69-year-old from Berlin systematically drugged and raped 14 women and filmed the assaults. A further 44 cases are expected to be examined in a separate trial.

entries1.title: Netenyahu's Likud party alleges interference and fraud in Israel's election
entries1.summary: Qatar has denied interfering in the election or funding efforts to influence the result, calling the accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”.

entries1.title: Palestinian President Abbas signals readiness for talks with Israel, seeks Cyprus mediation
entries1.summary: During his visit to Cyprus, the president of the Palestinian Authority Mahmoud Abbas said he is ready for talks with Israel's new government.

entries1.title: ‘I cannot remain neutral’: Lagarde finally explains her early ECB exit
entries1.summary: Lagarde says she is leaving the ECB early because she can no longer stay neutral. She also revealed the ECB debated a hike and hinted at a December move.

entries1.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display
entries1.summary: From silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, eight historic popemobiles go on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.

entries1.title: Europeans still worry about climate change – but are losing faith in EU green policies
entries1.summary: A new international poll reveals a widening gap between concern about climate change and confidence in the policies designed to tackle it, as EU governments struggle to reconcile ambitious green targets with mounting pressure to cut energy bills.

entries1.title: Brussels hopes unspent defence loans may help plug Ukraine’s budget hole
entries1.summary: The European Commission has reopened €21.3bn in unspent SAFE defence loans, urging EU governments to use them for joint projects with Ukraine, which faces a €70bn budget gap. Brussels cannot force them, but hopes the joint procurement rules will steer some of the money to Kyiv.

entries1.title: Mistral releases latest AI model for download, giving companies more control over their cybersecurity
entries1.summary: The French AI company says its Large 4 model offers advanced coding and cyber-defence capabilities and can be run on an organisation’s own computers and servers.

entries1.title: ‘I’m not a candidate for anything’: What Lagarde told Euronews before quitting the ECB
entries1.summary: Christine Lagarde told Euronews in an exclusive interview in July that she was not a candidate for any political office. Her announcement that she will leave the European Central Bank early, in February 2027, comes just months before France’s presidential election.

entries1.title: You Only Audition Once: Which actors came close to being cast as James Bond?
entries1.summary: James Bond is one of Hollywood’s most coveted roles, and some very famous actors came close to playing 007. As we wait for the identity of the seventh actor to land the role, here's a look back at the Bonds we never got.

entries1.title: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
entries1.summary: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

entries1.title: After the victory: The foreign policy and governing challenges facing Serbia’s student movement
entries1.summary: The victory of Serbia’s Student List has fundamentally changed the country’s political landscape. But winning the election may prove to have been the easier part.

entries1.title: Rembrandt's masterpieces become tattoos in the Netherlands
entries1.summary: Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art, permanently tattooed on their skin.

entries1.title: JD Vance contacts senior Iranian official in bid to revive peace talks
entries1.summary: With less than a week until the US congressional midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal has reported that JD Vance has written to Mohsen Rezaei in a bid to revive negotiations, as Trump continues to warn of possible renewed strikes again

entries1.title: NATO allies fear Trump will delay Patriot missiles for Ukraine until after US midterms
entries1.summary: Ukraine has called on US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth to sign off on the delivery of crucial Patriot defence systems used to intercept Russian ballistic missiles. But NATO sources warn the situation is "unpredictable."

entries1.title: ECB holds rates at 2.5% as Lagarde announces early exit with inflation near double the target
entries1.summary: The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday, hours after President Christine Lagarde said she would leave next February, months before her term ends, as France's bond market turmoil and inflation at 3.8% cloud the outlook for the eurozone.

entries1.title: Europe’s own ICE? Inside Brussels plans to triple Frontex and expand deportation powers
entries1.summary: The European Commission wants to triple Frontex's workforce and give it sweeping new powers to deport migrants beyond EU borders and monitor social media, prompting warnings over surveillance and fundamental rights.

entries1.title: US vs China: As the world splits into AI blocs, where does Europe stand?
entries1.summary: As the US and China build rival AI blocs, Europe is scrambling to reduce its dependence on both. But despite its ambitions to become a technological power in its own right, the EU still lacks the chips, infrastructure and homegrown AI models to compete on equal terms.

entries1.title: EU lawmakers press Beijing to rein in exports during Beijing visit
entries1.summary: Following a deal to curb Chinese hybrid car imports, EU lawmakers are demanding similar measures in other industrial sectors, warning that Beijing's export-driven economic model threatens European jobs and industries.

entries1.title: Nothing beats a Jet2… charter? Low-cost airline unveils business class-only plane
entries1.summary: The Boeing 737-800NG has 76 business class seats and is based out of Liverpool John Lennon Airport.

entries1.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian railway station kills at least 14 people
entries1.summary: Russia and Ukraine have intensified drone and missile attacks in recent months, even as Moscow and Kyiv prepare to resume US-mediated peace talks next month.

entries1.title: Watch: Fuel crisis strands 200 passengers aboard luxury cruise ship Odyssey
entries1.summary: Around 200 passengers on a residential cruise ship have been left stranded in Cambodia after its operator suspended operations amid soaring fuel costs. The MV Odyssey began its continuous world voyage from Belfast in October 2024, with some residents paying six figures for cabins.

entries1.title: Spain train crash: What happened in the 17 minutes before the collision?
entries1.summary: An IT failure halted several trains on the Madrid–Seville high-speed line, but the crash came after Adif’s control centre authorised an AVE to resume its journey. Investigators are examining what caused the collision, which killed 69 people.

entries1.title: Is von der Leyen’s ‘associate membership’ for Canada already dead?
entries1.summary: The term ‘associate membership’ was dropped from the EU-Canada summit text after German pushback, in a major blow to Commission President von der Leyen. Nonetheless, the two sides are still keen to boost their partnership.

entries1.title: Israel: protesters demand Arab-Jewish unity government after election
entries1.summary: Protesters took to the streets of Tel Aviv to demand a government bringing together Jewish and Arab parties. With Israel's election producing no clear winner, police moved in to disperse activists blocking traffic.

entries1.title: Ex-US Ambassador to NATO: Trump fears midterm defeat
entries1.summary: The former US Ambassador to NATO Kurt Volker told Euronews that the reason the US is delaying the delivery of Patriot missiles to Ukraine is because it may resume its war against Iran after the midterm elections.

entries1.title: Latest news bulletin | October 29th, 2026 – Midday
entries1.summary: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 29th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

entries1.title: Spain: cranes clear twisted train wreckage as rescuers work through the night
entries1.summary: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision that killed 68 people near Toledo. Cranes continued clearing the wreckage as authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify victims.

entries1.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down next February, months before her mandate ends
entries1.summary: Christine Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027, around nine months before the end of her eight-year term, the European Central Bank announced on Thursday, hours before it kept interest rates on hold at 2.5%.

entries1.title: In Pompeii, a woman's wardrobe resurfaces with beauty items and jewels
entries1.summary: Jewels, coins, tools and cosmetics: a cupboard in Cornelius Maximus's house brings to life the daily lives of Pompeii's women before Vesuvius erupted in AD 79.

entries1.title: US measles surge reminds of Europe’s vaccination gaps
entries1.summary: The US risks losing its measles elimination status as under-vaccinated communities across Europe remain vulnerable to imported cases.

entries1.title: What worker guarantees do unions and lawmakers demand to unblock EU Inc?
entries1.summary: Trade unions say the Commission’s pledge that labour law is “unaffected” does not close loopholes in the flagship 28th regime. Lawmakers cannot agree on how to fix them.

entries1.title: More refineries 'spread across the globe' needed to avoid disruptions during wars, says expert
entries1.summary: Energy expert and analyst Osama Rizvi believes high fuel prices have become a “structural feature” of the market, warning that it could take months for supplies to recover and prices to fall.

entries1.title: Putin calls Elon Musk a 'genius' as Russia builds its own Starlink rival
entries1.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has praised Elon Musk as a “genius” for deploying thousands of satellites into orbit. Speaking in Moscow, Putin highlighted Russia’s efforts to develop its own satellite internet network to rival Musk’s Starlink.

entries1.title: The doctor will see you now: Noah Wyle crowned People magazine's 2026 Sexiest Man Alive
entries1.summary: The 55-year-old actor, best know for his roles in ER and The Pitt, has officially been named People's 2026 Sexiest Man Alive.

entries1.title: Albania adopts measures to impose fines up to €5,500 on people at protests that become violent
entries1.summary: The measures come into force immediately, but require parliamentary approval within 45 days to remain in effect.

entries1.title: Bahamas: King Charles III dances with locals during Caribbean visit
entries1.summary: King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.

entries1.title: 'Protection is working': Madeira scientists study how fishing bans are restoring ocean life
entries1.summary: Nearly 200 scientists are studying the marine environment off Madeira's Desertas Islands.

entries1.title: Trump an 'aspiring authoriarian', says US historian Allan Lichtman
entries1.summary: He warns that Americans should be "very much prepared" if US President Trump attempts to overturn the results "by any means at his disposal", given the President's poor polling ratings and potential effects on the Republican Party's results.

entries1.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Wicker' – 50 Shades Of Hay?
entries1.summary: This frequently amusing fairytale about emancipation is also a very sweet-natured story that isn't the raunchy sexcapade the viral trailers might have led you to believe...

entries1.title: A train wreck: Can Sánchez survive Spain’s latest crisis?
entries1.summary: Good morning. It’s Thursday and my name is Angela Skujins. On today’s docket: a deadly train crash rocks Spain, a very fraught EU-Canada summit starts in Montreal, and questions mount over where Ukraine’s Patriot interceptor missiles are. Let’s dive in.

entries1.title: Festive voyages: Europe’s top Christmas market river cruises to book in 2026
entries1.summary: Choose between a sailing along the Main, the Danube or the Rhine, getting your fix of mulled wine and roasted chestnuts on the way.

entries1.title: Volkswagen posts €5.8 billion loss as Chinese competition bites
entries1.summary: Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen said on Thursday it had made a €5.8 billion loss in the third quarter, as it struggles with intense Chinese competition.

entries1.title: Europe Today: Second high-speed rail disaster in nine months leaves Spain in grief
entries1.summary: At least 68 people died when two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid, Spain's second deadly rail crash this year. In Montreal, EU leaders meet Mark Carney to launch an 'Alliance for the Future'. We also look at next week's US midterms, Ukraine's defence capabilities, and rising oil prices.

entries1.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian drone strike kills 14 at Ukraine train station
entries1.summary: Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform and rescuers helping victims to safety.

entries1.title: Japan to aid wildfire recovery efforts in Mongolia
entries1.summary: Takaichi said Japan will offer an aid package featuring plans to provide equipment and help develop human resources for environmental restoration.

entries1.title: Hong Kong leader apologizes for deadly Tai Po fire, pledges reform
entries1.summary: Lee promised swift but extensive reforms to the city's building industry and regulatory system.

entries1.title: ECB President Lagarde resigns at time of mounting challenges for Europe
entries1.summary: The move comes as the ECB battles inflation risks from an Iran-driven oil shock while a sharp rise in bond yields threatens to dampen growth.

entries1.title: Toyota monthly sales fall as China slump enters eighth month
entries1.summary: China, the global auto industry's leading market, has proven difficult for the world's biggest carmaker.

entries1.title: A cruise ship was their home. Now residents of Villa Vie Odyssey must leave.
entries1.summary: The ship's hundreds of residents have been ordered to disembark in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, where it has been stranded because it can't afford fuel.

entries1.title: Ex-Takenaka manager admits breach of trust over Osaka Expo
entries1.summary: The former manager acknowledged having a subcontractor submit inflated bills for construction work related to last year's World Exposition.

entries1.summary: The investment underscores Japanese institutional investor interest in Indian companies across financial services, manufacturing and real estate.

entries1.title: LDP, JIP and DPP plan to cut Lower House seats, ending standoff
entries1.summary: The three parties plan to introduce and pass a related bill by the end of the current session to cut 31 proportional representation seats.

entries1.title: Politician ordered to pay ¥1.1 million for outing author as transgender
entries1.summary: A Tokyo court ruled that the disclosure of the author's assigned gender at birth without her consent was an unlawful invasion of privacy.

entries1.title: Taiwan says Pakistan briefly closed airspace to Taiwanese flights
entries1.summary: The island suspects China of being behind the unprecedented move.

entries1.title: Japan must accelerate cyberdefense strategy, former NSA director says
entries1.summary: Spending weeks and months on strategy is not conducive to an active cyberdefense posture, according to former intelligence chief Michael Rogers.

entries1.summary: A commentary in China's Global Times has accused the hit TBS drama series of vilifying the country.

entries1.title: GMO cybersecurity team finds info critical to identifying hackers, CEO says
entries1.summary: The hacker group has remained publicly silent since its website revealing GMO client personal data was taken down Wednesday.

entries1.title: Naomi Osaka upset by 144th-ranked Mia Pohankova at Pan Pacific Open

entries1.title: Hungary’s post-Orban shakeout ripples through auto industry
entries1.summary: Its tougher line on environmental enforcement comes at a time when the former prime minister's bet on electric cars is starting to pay off.

entries1.title: ‘Stupid Never Dies’: A zombie B-movie resurrected in game form
entries1.summary: There's morbid charm to this undead roguelite, but the real terror is in its uneven approach to a genre with plenty of polished gems.

entries1.title: Company executives and Chinese national held over visa fraud
entries1.summary: One of the executives is believed to have submitted fraudulent applications for visas for between 30 and 40 Chinese nationals beginning in 2020.

entries1.summary: The social media platform founded by the U.S. president is said to sell speedier access to his content for up to $100,000 a month.

entries1.title: Airbus ready for linkup with GCAP, CEO says
entries1.summary: Joining the British-Japanese-Italian consortium to build a next-generation fighter jet is an option after the collapse of a Franco-German rival.

entries1.title: Chiefs add kicker Justin Tucker to practice squad as Harrison Butker struggles
entries1.summary: Tucker was released by the Baltimore Ravens in May 2025 amid declining production and allegations from 16 massage therapists who had accused him of sexual misconduct.

entries1.summary: The better path is harder but more defensible: preserve the court, reform its operation and confront the limits of international law honestly.
