entries1.title: AFTER THE BELL: Why are SA’s cannabis rules still up in smoke?
entries1.summary: Eight years after a court ruling, South Africa still lacks workable cannabis rules, frustrating consumers, businesses and efforts to bring the industry into the formal economy.

entries1.title: GEOPOLITICS OP-ED: Brazil’s election — a victory for Lula, a wake-up call for democracy
entries1.summary: Lula’s narrow victory matters far beyond Brazil. It represents Brazil’s place in a fractured world while questioning whether the country can finally convert extraordinary potential into prosperity. But the message from voters and a right-leaning legislature is clear: political history and ideological loyalties are no substitute for delivery.

entries1.title: OBITUARY: Paris Mashile — regulator who fought to make SA’s phone calls cheaper
entries1.summary: The engineer, political activist and Shakespeare lover turned the technical machinery of communications into a public argument about power, access and accountability.

entries1.title: Watch – The pipeline between US white supremacists and the SA right
THE FINANCIAL WELLNESS COACH: Interest on your money in the bank may deliver less than expected after tax
entries1.summary: It’s worth exploring investment options, offshore endowments and estate planning to reduce costs and avoid a hefty SA Revenue Service bill.

entries1.title: What it takes to fight increasingly sophisticated, AI-powered disinformation campaigns
entries1.summary: Veteran defender of fact-based journalism and founder of the BBC’s Trusted News Initiative, Jessica Cecil, recently launched a new publication about disinformation. These are her reflections on Athena’s first month in the trenches of the information war.

entries1.title: SPY TRIAL : EFF secures Zuma-era SSA spy records as Idac stands by R12m case
entries1.summary: More than a decade after the State Security Agency (SSA) allegedly infiltrated its ranks, the EFF has secured access to court records detailing how the party was targeted and infiltrated. This comes as the two men accused in the R12-million Project Mayibuye case prepare to ask the court to discharge them without presenting a defence.

entries1.title: HOSTING AMBITIONS: SA unveils Durban as candidate city in its bid to host the Olympic Games
entries1.summary: The South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee has identified Durban as its preferred host city in its bid to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic Games. But questions remain about the country’s readiness.

entries1.title: POLITICALLY AWEH: Six parties share how they’ll tackle the cost of living
entries1.summary: In episode two of Politically Aweh’s Elections Showdown mini-series, we ask six political party representatives about the cost of living – including transportation costs, electricity tariffs, and municipal rates.

entries1.title: El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti for rescue while elections postponed
entries1.summary: El Salvador will send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to rescue missing personnel and support anti-gang security operations, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, while Haiti's electoral council postponed planned presidential elections to next year.

entries1.title: Taiwan flags ‘obvious’ threat from 50 Chinese vessels in wide sweep of waters
entries1.summary: China has more than 50 navy and other official vessels operating in a wide swath of sea stretching from southern Japan down to Taiwan and off the Philippines, a senior Taiwan official said, calling the threat level "obvious"

entries1.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles toward sea off east coast, Seoul says
entries1.summary: North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Thursday, South Korea's military said, as tensions run high ahead of Pyongyang's end-of-month deadline to activate propaganda loudspeakers along the heavily armed border.

entries1.title: ANALYSIS: So you want to govern a metro? Be careful what you wish for
entries1.summary: The Electoral Commission says 546 parties are contesting these elections, claiming to want to be part of governing our councils and metros. They should think very carefully about that.

entries1.title: HOUSEHOLD SQUEEZE: Fuel levy cut offers brief relief as food basket outpaces SA’s unchanged SRD grant
entries1.summary: High fuel prices are squeezing South African household budgets, while the R370 Social Relief of Distress grant still falls short of the cost of a basic food basket.

entries1.title: WHAT’S COOKING: Rich, fruity Christmas cake
entries1.summary: Fruit, nuts, spices and strong liquor — that’s the recipe for the kind of traditional Christmas cake that is made two months in advance. This is the one we made a year ago, and now is the best time to get yours made. It’s best to make a family occasion of it, creating memories along with a cake to look forward to.

entries1.title: BOOK EXCERPT: Sandstone Estates – where steam locomotives bring SA railway history to life
entries1.summary: Trains, planes, automobiles, tanks and tractors will all gather at Sandstone Estates in the Eastern Free State in mid-November to celebrate the magic of old machines and cherries.

entries1.title: AMABHUNGANE: Takeover row: Butters vs the Takeover Regulation Panel — and Warren Chapman
entries1.summary: The Takeover Regulation Panel is supposed to protect minority shareholders. Did it fold under pressure when confronting broker Peresec and its powerful boss Warren Chapman? Activist shareholder Craig Butters is making that claim in a high-stakes court case.

entries1.title: Alphabet stock sinks as search woes cause revenue miss, cash burn worsens
entries1.summary: Oct 28 (Reuters) - Google parent Alphabet reported disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn as it poured resources into building out AI.

entries1.title: Leak website releases data on thousands of US Homeland Security employees
entries1.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 28 (Reuters) - The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.

entries1.title: Judge rejects US Justice Dept bid to block votes from alleged noncitizens in California
entries1.summary: Oct 28 (Reuters) - A US judge strongly rebuked the Trump administration on Wednesday by rejecting a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting mail ballots for the midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the department alleges are likely noncitizens.

entries1.title: After landing in US, Flavio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil’s rightful leader
entries1.summary: SAO PAULO, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Senator Flavio Bolsonaro declared himself Brazil's rightful leader on Wednesday after arriving in the United States, alleging he was the victim of an electoral coup by the country's Supreme Court and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won the vote by over 4 million votes.

entries1.title: ANALYSIS: Treasury faces high-stakes battle on the road to social safety net grant reform
entries1.summary: South Africa operates one of the largest social assistance systems in the developing world. The broader social wage – including spending on education, healthcare and other social services – accounts for over 60% of government expenditure. Of course there will be resistance to any change.

entries1.title: PROJECT MAYIBUYE: SSA operation targeting EFF lacked national security basis, court told
entries1.summary: Project Mayibuye should have been stopped before it started. Instead, the Gauteng High Court heard, the secret State Security Agency operation went ahead, targeted the EFF and had millions channelled through it.

entries1.title: STING OPERATION: SA ‘refugee’ in US faces decades behind bars on child sexual exploitation charges
entries1.summary: The American Dream of ‘refugee’ Arno Venter has come crashing down after just four months with his arrest and indictment on 11 charges involving child sexual abuse material.

entries1.title: Watch — Frank Chikane, DA polls and the ANC’s retreat from the cities
XENOBAROMETER: Ugandan man nearly killed by March and March mob speaks from hospital
entries1.summary: ‘Simon’, recovering in hospital after a Durban mob attack, recounts fleeing masked protesters and losing consciousness as concerns grow over anti-immigrant violence in 2026.

entries1.title: TRC Roulette : Apartheid’s scapegoat — the jarring paradox of mass killer Eugene de Kock
entries1.summary: Testifying at the Khampepe Inquiry, the former Vlakplaas commander lays bare how political interference and a ‘rotten system’ shielded the generals while leaving him to take the fall alone.

entries1.title: CRIMEFIGHTING REFORM: R1bn in recovered loot to fund Firoz Cachalia’s police reset
entries1.summary: Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia says money taken from criminals is funding the fight against organised crime, while broad reforms are under way to depoliticise the police, rebuild Crime Intelligence and clean up SAPS procurement processes.

entries1.title: GOVERNANCE FIASCO OP-ED: Bronkhorstspruit gastro outbreak: A failure to keep people safe
entries1.summary: With 833 people seeking treatment, Bronkhorstspruit’s outbreak highlights how failures in water treatment and government leadership put vulnerable communities at risk.

entries1.title: Yawn-fest — political parties bore voters with dull election slogans, poles show
entries1.summary: Voters are being bored to death by pathetic political party slogans and posters as we head for the seminal 4 November local government elections.

entries1.title: DOUBLE TROUBLE: Suliman Carrim granted R100K bail in Madlanga case, but remains jailed on car-smuggling charges
entries1.summary: North West businessman Suliman Carrim was granted bail for failing to continue testifying at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry. However, he remains behind bars on separate car-smuggling charges, in a case where two of his co-accused may plead guilty.

entries1.title: Markets are waking up to the risks they have spent months ignoring
entries1.summary: Markets are showing signs of a major shift as concerns over inflated AI valuations, economic growth and interest rates drive investors away from equities and towards government bonds. Upcoming central bank signals and tech earnings could determine whether markets stabilise or face a deeper sell-off in the months ahead.

entries1.title: As Trump staggers to the polls, Americans yearning for change prepare to say ‘enough’
entries1.summary: It is hard to fully describe the epic destruction Trump has wrought, and next Tuesday the Americans will deliver a verdict on all of it – and it doesn’t look good for him. His name might not be on any ballot on 3 November, but the election is a referendum on his presidency.

entries1.title: Fuel levy remedy: Relief for a month, pressure for a lifetime
entries1.summary: The 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement offers a welcome pause at the petrol pump, but mistakes temporary relief for a durable answer to South Africa’s cost-of-living crisis.

entries1.title: Right of reply: SA needs more factories, not more walls
entries1.summary: Chinese electric vehicles and investment can boost South African manufacturing, create jobs and accelerate the affordable green transition, while tariffs risk harming consumers and businesses. South Africa should protect its economic sovereignty and maintain strong trade ties with both China and the European Union.

entries1.title: Wildlife is not livestock — Aucamp’s dangerous plan to turn conservation into agriculture
entries1.summary: Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp wants South Africa’s wildlife ranching industry transferred to his department. Behind the rhetoric of economic growth and sustainable use lies a potentially far-reaching attempt to redefine wildlife as an agricultural commodity, raising serious constitutional, ecological and ethical questions.

entries1.title: There is another Afrikaner story worth telling, rooted in reconciliation and a shared future
entries1.summary: While much of the international discussion about Afrikaners focuses on fear and persecution, there are people whose lives tell a different story about our place in South Africa.

entries1.title: Mantashe shifts focus from women’s vulnerability to linguistic legitimacy
entries1.summary: The debate around Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe’s remarks about women seeking job opportunities being asked for sexual favours by men occupying positions of authority has turned into a discussion about language, and obscures the original question put to him concerning allegations of exploitation and power.

entries1.title: The other Pillay at the Geneva pharmacy
entries1.summary: A surname coincidence in Switzerland brings back memories of my parents’ generation, and the opportunities opened to some women and denied to others.

entries1.title: East African Crude Oil Pipeline financing: Can Standard Bank’s climate claims survive scrutiny
entries1.summary: Standard Bank cannot market itself as a champion of human rights and green progress while it bankrolls environmental destruction and community dispossession in east Africa. This matter is now before South Africa’s Advertising Regulatory Board.

entries1.title: Regulation of religion — SA must tackle religious abuse without restricting freedom of belief
entries1.summary: On International Religious Freedom Day, the biggest threat facing religious freedom in SA is an institution created to protect it.

entries1.title: Dealing with conservation’s inconvenient individual
entries1.summary: Conservation may save species, but what does it cost individual animals? Welfare belongs in the ethical calculus: sustainable is not always ethically justified.

entries1.title: Local elections 2026: How do you choose who to vote for?
entries1.summary: Local elections are about more than party loyalty: scrutinise candidates, understand the job and decide what accountability should look like five years from now.

entries1.title: Why the best-laid plans to fix Joburg won’t work — and what will
entries1.summary: Fixing our municipalities requires more than listing obvious infrastructural failures. True recovery demands structural debt relief, national-level support and clear operational strategies to allow incoming leadership a fresh starting point to rebuild.

entries1.title: When the state fails to protect you, self-defence isn’t a luxury; it’s a necessity
entries1.summary: Amid a failure of state protection, disarming law-abiding citizens through the Firearms Control Amendment Bill and ignoring the Private Security Industry Regulatory Authority’s governance crisis will fuel chaos rather than safety.

entries1.title: El Niño threatens to deepen southern Africa’s poverty crisis
entries1.summary: An expected El Niño drought, rising costs and shrinking humanitarian aid could worsen food insecurity and poverty across southern Africa in 2027. South Africa’s strong grain harvest and water reserves offer some protection, but regional food shortages may increase pressure on supplies and exports.

entries1.title: Lula’s Brazil election win has given the world breathing space
entries1.summary: Lula da Silva’s historic fourth-term victory in Brazil signals hope for multilateralism, climate action and the Global South. With profound geopolitical implications for global sovereignty, it also presents a crucial opportunity for South Africa.

entries1.title: Watch – Top Court puts ANC candidates back on ballot after missed deadline
Watch - Ramaphosa’s reform message as polls show continued ANC decline
Watch – Ferial Haffajee and Ernst Roets on Agoa, crosses and autonomy

entries2.title: AFTER THE BELL: Why are SA’s cannabis rules still up in smoke?
entries2.summary: Eight years after a court ruling, South Africa still lacks workable cannabis rules, frustrating consumers, businesses and efforts to bring the industry into the formal economy.

entries2.title: GEOPOLITICS OP-ED: Brazil’s election — a victory for Lula, a wake-up call for democracy
entries2.summary: Lula’s narrow victory matters far beyond Brazil. It represents Brazil’s place in a fractured world while questioning whether the country can finally convert extraordinary potential into prosperity. But the message from voters and a right-leaning legislature is clear: political history and ideological loyalties are no substitute for delivery.

entries2.title: OBITUARY: Paris Mashile — regulator who fought to make SA’s phone calls cheaper
entries2.summary: The engineer, political activist and Shakespeare lover turned the technical machinery of communications into a public argument about power, access and accountability.

entries2.title: Watch – The pipeline between US white supremacists and the SA right
THE FINANCIAL WELLNESS COACH: Interest on your money in the bank may deliver less than expected after tax
entries2.summary: It’s worth exploring investment options, offshore endowments and estate planning to reduce costs and avoid a hefty SA Revenue Service bill.

entries2.title: What it takes to fight increasingly sophisticated, AI-powered disinformation campaigns
entries2.summary: Veteran defender of fact-based journalism and founder of the BBC’s Trusted News Initiative, Jessica Cecil, recently launched a new publication about disinformation. These are her reflections on Athena’s first month in the trenches of the information war.

entries2.title: SPY TRIAL : EFF secures Zuma-era SSA spy records as Idac stands by R12m case
entries2.summary: More than a decade after the State Security Agency (SSA) allegedly infiltrated its ranks, the EFF has secured access to court records detailing how the party was targeted and infiltrated. This comes as the two men accused in the R12-million Project Mayibuye case prepare to ask the court to discharge them without presenting a defence.

entries2.title: HOSTING AMBITIONS: SA unveils Durban as candidate city in its bid to host the Olympic Games
entries2.summary: The South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee has identified Durban as its preferred host city in its bid to host the 2036 or 2040 Olympic Games. But questions remain about the country’s readiness.

entries2.title: POLITICALLY AWEH: Six parties share how they’ll tackle the cost of living
entries2.summary: In episode two of Politically Aweh’s Elections Showdown mini-series, we ask six political party representatives about the cost of living – including transportation costs, electricity tariffs, and municipal rates.

entries2.title: El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti for rescue while elections postponed
entries2.summary: El Salvador will send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to rescue missing personnel and support anti-gang security operations, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, while Haiti's electoral council postponed planned presidential elections to next year.

entries2.title: Taiwan flags ‘obvious’ threat from 50 Chinese vessels in wide sweep of waters
entries2.summary: China has more than 50 navy and other official vessels operating in a wide swath of sea stretching from southern Japan down to Taiwan and off the Philippines, a senior Taiwan official said, calling the threat level "obvious"

entries2.title: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles toward sea off east coast, Seoul says
entries2.summary: North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Thursday, South Korea's military said, as tensions run high ahead of Pyongyang's end-of-month deadline to activate propaganda loudspeakers along the heavily armed border.

entries2.title: ANALYSIS: So you want to govern a metro? Be careful what you wish for
entries2.summary: The Electoral Commission says 546 parties are contesting these elections, claiming to want to be part of governing our councils and metros. They should think very carefully about that.

entries1.title: Cubans call for lifting of embargo, express hope for better lives
entries1.summary: Cuban citizens expressed hope that the US will respond to the calls of the international community as soon as possible and voiced their wishes for better lives, after the United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution for the 34th consecutive time urging the US to end its embargo.

entries1.title: DRC: US sanctions on Rwanda draw mixed reactions in Goma
entries1.summary: In Goma, some residents want to believe that this additional pressure could help break the deadlock. Michel Kamango hopes the sanctions will affect the parties concerned and help bring about a return to peace.

entries1.title: Putin hails 'natural allies' at Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
entries1.summary: President Putin welcomed nearly two dozen African leaders to the Kremlin on Wednesday for a two-day Russia-Africa summit.

entries1.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display
entries1.summary: From silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, eight historic popemobiles go on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.

entries1.title: French music producer awaits trial six years after police beating
entries1.summary: Six years after being violently beaten by three police officers, Michel Zecler is awaiting the opening of their trial on 9 November in Paris. The music producer says he remains deeply scarred and angry over police violence.

entries1.title: Gabon oil rig disaster: Three bodies found, two still missing
entries1.summary: Three bodies have been found following the sinking of an oil rig off the coast of Gabon on Saturday, while the search continues for two people still missing, according to an updated toll released by Gabonese authorities overnight from Wednesday to Thursday.

entries1.title: DRC Ebola clinic celebrates departure of last confirmed cases
entries1.summary: Medical staff were joined by local residents as they celebrated the departure of the last Ebola patients from a treatment center in DR Congo’s Ituri province. It’s the first time the Médicins Sans Frontières-run clinic has had no confirmed Ebola cases since the outbreak was declared in May.

entries1.title: A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, victims still await justice
entries1.summary: A year after Tanzania's bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.

entries1.title: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
entries1.summary: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

entries1.title: Rembrandt's masterpieces become tattoos in the Netherlands
entries1.summary: Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art, permanently tattooed on their skin.

entries1.title: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world
entries1.summary: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world

entries1.title: Cameroonian opposition parties condemn the suspension of Issa Tchiroma’s party
entries1.summary: Cameroonian opposition parties condemned the three-month suspension of Issa Tchiroma Bakary’s political party, the National Salvation Front of Cameroon.

entries1.title: Senegal: What strategies to tackle the debt? [Business Africa]
entries1.summary: Senegal is stepping up negotiations with international creditors to ease its public debt burden, estimated at nearly 130% of GDP in 2025, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

entries1.title: Brazilians divided after defeated candidate Bolsonaro flees to US
entries1.summary: As Brazilian media reported the news that defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro had fled to the US, public opinion remained divided. The 45-year-old former senator is under investigation over allegations of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion.

entries1.title: Ghana says Russia has backed its bid to join BRICS as a partner country
entries1.summary: Accra is seeking partner status in the bloc of emerging economies, hoping to attract investment, expand trade, and strengthen its economy.

entries1.title: Israel: protesters demand Arab-Jewish unity government after election
entries1.summary: Protesters took to the streets of Tel Aviv to demand a government bringing together Jewish and Arab parties. With Israel's election producing no clear winner, police moved in to disperse activists blocking traffic.

entries1.title: Tunisian journalist sentenced to four years in jail on terrorism charges
entries1.summary: International journalism organisations have condemned Zied el-Heni's conviction on terrorism offenses saying its an escalation of Tunisia's assault on the press.

entries1.title: Libya's eastern administration bans nationals from Iran and Afghanistan
entries1.summary: Libya’s Government of National Stability that controls the country’s east has barred citizens of Iran and Afghanistan from entering its territory.

entries1.title: Spain: cranes clear twisted train wreckage as rescuers work through the night
entries1.summary: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision that killed 68 people near Toledo. Cranes continued clearing the wreckage as authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify victims.

entries1.title: 6 million in Haiti face severe hunger amid violence, displacement and El Niño
entries1.summary: Aid organisations in Haiti are introducing a new programme to help people get enough to eat. Nearly six million people in the Caribbean nation are experiencing severe hunger, according to a new UN-backed report. Almost two million are facing emergency levels of food insecurity.

entries1.title: US imposes sanctions on Rwandan defence ministry over links to Congo rebels
entries1.summary: Washington hopes to increase pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops from the DRC and end support for the M23 group.

entries1.title: Bahamas: King Charles III dances with locals during Caribbean visit
entries1.summary: King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.

entries1.title: Calls for slavery reparations grow louder as British king visits Caribbean
entries1.summary: King Charles III's nine-day visit is being overshadowed by increasingly vocal demands for Britain to pay for its role in the slave trade.

entries1.title: Russia-Africa Summit: Putin seeks to expand ties with the continent
entries1.summary: At the plenary session, Vladimir Putin told delegates that Moscow was Africa's best partner, calling for an end to Western domination.

entries1.title: Spain: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night
entries1.summary: Spain reels from the deadly Toledo high-speed train collision that killed 68 and injured more than 100, sparking grief, protests and calls for resignations.

entries1.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel hope election results bring change
entries1.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel expressed optimism on Wednesday following the strong showing of Arab parties in the elections.

entries1.title: Recreatrales festival transforms Ouagadougou neighbourhood
entries1.summary: In Ouagadougou, an entire neighbourhood brings the Récréâtrales theatre festival to life. For its 14th edition, running from October 24 to 31, residents of Bougsemtenga are hosting performances in their courtyards.

entries1.title: Africa Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, mostly in DR Congo
entries1.summary: Africa's latest outbreak of Ebola has passed 10,000 confirmed cases, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Congolese health authorities said on Tuesday, with almost 5,000 fatalities.

entries1.title: King Charles III's Caribbean tour renews calls for UK slavery reparations
entries1.summary: The British king begins a tour of the Caribbean today, during which he will visit several former British colonies. It has renewed calls for the UK to apologies and pay reparations for its role in the slave trade.

entries1.title: Oil slick from Strait of Hormuz reaches UAE's northern coast
entries1.summary: An oil slick from a tanker attacked in the Strait of Hormuz has reached the United Arab Emirates.

entries1.title: Spain: Rescuers search mangled train wreckage near Toledo
entries1.summary: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens more injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, in central Spain’s Toledo province, on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities warned the toll could rise further as rescuers searched the wreckage.

entries1.title: Humanitarian situation worsening in Sudan's camps for displaced people
entries1.summary: Displaced and official at Al-Karama 3 camp in the city of El-Damazin in Sudan's Blue Nile state say the humanitarian conditions are deteriorating in the camp, as war rages in the country. "The camp hasn't received any food aid for four months now," says the camp's manager.

entries1.title: Bolsonaro’s son and family flee to Miami after refusing to concede
entries1.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Monday after leaving Brazil, following his defeat in the presidential election.

entries1.title: Britain's King Charles III attends youth rally in the Bahamas
entries1.summary: Britain’s King Charles III on Tuesday addressed a youth gathering at Clifford Park in Nassau, recalling the Bahamas’ independence celebrations in 1973 and highlighting the country’s cultural achievements and vulnerability to climate change.

entries1.title: South Sudan independence figure Joseph Lagu dies aged 94
entries1.summary: South Sudan is observing national mourning on Wednesday following the death of Joseph Lagu, a key figure in the independence of the world's youngest country, who told AFP that he began his fight armed with only "a machete".

entries1.title: Tanzania announces first major natural gas discovery in a decade
entries1.summary: Tanzania has announced its first natural gas discovery in a decade, with an estimated 223 billion cubic feet found at the Kasa-1X ST2 well in the Mnazi Bay area.

entries1.title: Pix of the Day, 28th October, 2026 - Across the world
entries1.summary: Pix of the Day, 28th October, 2026 - Across the world

entries1.title: South African activists push back on data centre rush
entries1.summary: Civil society groups have demanded a halt in the construction of new AI centres in South Africa. The prospect of a water- and power-hungry hyperscale data centre near areas of the city where thousands of people lack proper access to these resources has alarmed activists.

entries1.title: Russia's President Putin hosts counterparts from Mozambique, Libya and Equatorial Guinea
entries1.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met for talks with counterparts from Mozambique, Libya and Equatorial Guinea in Moscow on Tuesday following the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.

entries1.title: Nigeria's Dangote oil refinery closes 'historic' IPO
entries1.summary: Africa's largest ever initial public offering closed on Wednesday after raising funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate.

entries1.title: Spain: First footage reveals wreckage of deadly high-speed train crash
entries1.summary: At least 10 people died when a high-speed train struck another near Toledo, Spain. Two carriages derailed, leaving rescuers searching through the wreckage as authorities warned the death toll could rise.

entries1.title: Whereabouts of Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Bolsonaro unknown
entries1.summary: The whereabouts of Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro were unknown on Wednesday after reports that he fled the country. Bolsonaro lost the runoff election to incumbent Luis Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday but has refused to concede defeat.

entries1.title: No clear winner in Israel's first election since the 2023 Hamas attack
entries1.summary: The vote has widely been seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s handling of the conflict, with turnout the highest in decades.

entries1.title: Judge throws out attempted murder case against Zimbabwe VP's ex-wife
entries1.summary: After 7 years on remand, the ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice president walked out of a Harare prison on Tuesday after a judge ordered her release. Marry Mubaiwa had been accused of attempting to murder her former husband Constantino Chiwenga in 2019.

entries1.title: Sana'a factory in flames as Houthis, government forces exchange strikes
entries1.summary: Houthi media reported that Saudi-backed government forces have launched airstrikes on a "Hamdan" cement factory in Sana'a on Tuesday.

entries1.title: Brazil: Lula celebrates 81st birthday after re-election victory
entries1.summary: Brazil's re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October, with dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília, just two days after winning a closely contested election.

entries1.title: Ukraine: massive fire engulfs buildings after Russian strike on Kharkiv
entries1.summary: Five people, including a 4-year-old child, were injured in an overnight Russian drone strike on Kharkiv. The attack set several buildings ablaze, with firefighters working under the threat of further strikes.

entries1.title: Senegal's finance committee to review revised budget key to IMF deal
entries1.summary: The country has been grappling with a debt burden that the IMF says had reached 132 per cent of gross domestic product by ⁠the end of 2024.

entries1.title: Iranian president says Middle East can solve its problems without  United States
entries1.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian made the comments during talks with Russia's President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum in Moscow.

entries1.title: Israel: opposition supporters celebrate narrow lead in exit polls
entries1.summary: Supporters of Gadi Eisenkot celebrated in Tel Aviv as exit polls gave Israel's opposition bloc a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, but no outright parliamentary majority.

entries2.title: Cubans call for lifting of embargo, express hope for better lives
entries2.summary: Cuban citizens expressed hope that the US will respond to the calls of the international community as soon as possible and voiced their wishes for better lives, after the United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution for the 34th consecutive time urging the US to end its embargo.

entries2.title: DRC: US sanctions on Rwanda draw mixed reactions in Goma
entries2.summary: In Goma, some residents want to believe that this additional pressure could help break the deadlock. Michel Kamango hopes the sanctions will affect the parties concerned and help bring about a return to peace.

entries2.title: Putin hails 'natural allies' at Russia-Africa summit in Moscow
entries2.summary: President Putin welcomed nearly two dozen African leaders to the Kremlin on Wednesday for a two-day Russia-Africa summit.

entries2.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display
entries2.summary: From silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, eight historic popemobiles go on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.

entries2.title: French music producer awaits trial six years after police beating
entries2.summary: Six years after being violently beaten by three police officers, Michel Zecler is awaiting the opening of their trial on 9 November in Paris. The music producer says he remains deeply scarred and angry over police violence.

entries2.title: Gabon oil rig disaster: Three bodies found, two still missing
entries2.summary: Three bodies have been found following the sinking of an oil rig off the coast of Gabon on Saturday, while the search continues for two people still missing, according to an updated toll released by Gabonese authorities overnight from Wednesday to Thursday.

entries2.title: DRC Ebola clinic celebrates departure of last confirmed cases
entries2.summary: Medical staff were joined by local residents as they celebrated the departure of the last Ebola patients from a treatment center in DR Congo’s Ituri province. It’s the first time the Médicins Sans Frontières-run clinic has had no confirmed Ebola cases since the outbreak was declared in May.

entries2.title: A year after Tanzania’s bloody election, victims still await justice
entries2.summary: A year after Tanzania's bloody election, many remain traumatised by the violence, while government critics live in fear of abduction and arbitrary arrest, or facing treason and terrorism charges.

entries2.title: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
entries2.summary: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

entries2.title: Rembrandt's masterpieces become tattoos in the Netherlands
entries2.summary: Visitors to the Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, can once again take home a piece of the Dutch master's art, permanently tattooed on their skin.

entries2.title: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world
entries2.summary: Pix of the Day, 29th October, 2026 - Across the world

entries2.title: Cameroonian opposition parties condemn the suspension of Issa Tchiroma’s party
entries2.summary: Cameroonian opposition parties condemned the three-month suspension of Issa Tchiroma Bakary’s political party, the National Salvation Front of Cameroon.

entries2.title: Senegal: What strategies to tackle the debt? [Business Africa]
entries2.summary: Senegal is stepping up negotiations with international creditors to ease its public debt burden, estimated at nearly 130% of GDP in 2025, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

entries2.title: Brazilians divided after defeated candidate Bolsonaro flees to US
entries2.summary: As Brazilian media reported the news that defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro had fled to the US, public opinion remained divided. The 45-year-old former senator is under investigation over allegations of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion.

entries2.title: Ghana says Russia has backed its bid to join BRICS as a partner country
entries2.summary: Accra is seeking partner status in the bloc of emerging economies, hoping to attract investment, expand trade, and strengthen its economy.

entries2.title: Israel: protesters demand Arab-Jewish unity government after election
entries2.summary: Protesters took to the streets of Tel Aviv to demand a government bringing together Jewish and Arab parties. With Israel's election producing no clear winner, police moved in to disperse activists blocking traffic.

entries2.title: Tunisian journalist sentenced to four years in jail on terrorism charges
entries2.summary: International journalism organisations have condemned Zied el-Heni's conviction on terrorism offenses saying its an escalation of Tunisia's assault on the press.

entries2.title: Libya's eastern administration bans nationals from Iran and Afghanistan
entries2.summary: Libya’s Government of National Stability that controls the country’s east has barred citizens of Iran and Afghanistan from entering its territory.

entries2.title: Spain: cranes clear twisted train wreckage as rescuers work through the night
entries2.summary: Rescue teams worked through the night at the site of a train collision that killed 68 people near Toledo. Cranes continued clearing the wreckage as authorities set up a temporary morgue to identify victims.

entries2.title: 6 million in Haiti face severe hunger amid violence, displacement and El Niño
entries2.summary: Aid organisations in Haiti are introducing a new programme to help people get enough to eat. Nearly six million people in the Caribbean nation are experiencing severe hunger, according to a new UN-backed report. Almost two million are facing emergency levels of food insecurity.

entries2.title: US imposes sanctions on Rwandan defence ministry over links to Congo rebels
entries2.summary: Washington hopes to increase pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops from the DRC and end support for the M23 group.

entries2.title: Bahamas: King Charles III dances with locals during Caribbean visit
entries2.summary: King Charles III showed off his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October, as part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.

entries2.title: Calls for slavery reparations grow louder as British king visits Caribbean
entries2.summary: King Charles III's nine-day visit is being overshadowed by increasingly vocal demands for Britain to pay for its role in the slave trade.

entries2.title: Russia-Africa Summit: Putin seeks to expand ties with the continent
entries2.summary: At the plenary session, Vladimir Putin told delegates that Moscow was Africa's best partner, calling for an end to Western domination.

entries2.title: Spain: Madrid mourns train crash victims as rescuers work through the night
entries2.summary: Spain reels from the deadly Toledo high-speed train collision that killed 68 and injured more than 100, sparking grief, protests and calls for resignations.

entries2.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel hope election results bring change
entries2.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel expressed optimism on Wednesday following the strong showing of Arab parties in the elections.

entries2.title: Recreatrales festival transforms Ouagadougou neighbourhood
entries2.summary: In Ouagadougou, an entire neighbourhood brings the Récréâtrales theatre festival to life. For its 14th edition, running from October 24 to 31, residents of Bougsemtenga are hosting performances in their courtyards.

entries2.title: Africa Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, mostly in DR Congo
entries2.summary: Africa's latest outbreak of Ebola has passed 10,000 confirmed cases, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Congolese health authorities said on Tuesday, with almost 5,000 fatalities.

entries2.title: King Charles III's Caribbean tour renews calls for UK slavery reparations
entries2.summary: The British king begins a tour of the Caribbean today, during which he will visit several former British colonies. It has renewed calls for the UK to apologies and pay reparations for its role in the slave trade.

entries2.title: Oil slick from Strait of Hormuz reaches UAE's northern coast
entries2.summary: An oil slick from a tanker attacked in the Strait of Hormuz has reached the United Arab Emirates.

entries2.title: Spain: Rescuers search mangled train wreckage near Toledo
entries2.summary: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens more injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, in central Spain’s Toledo province, on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities warned the toll could rise further as rescuers searched the wreckage.

entries1.title: Late Lyon wicket puts Australia in control of deciding Test
entries1.summary: South Africa loses four wickets and has a lead of just 40 runs, as Nathan Lyon claims the crucial wicket of Temba Bavuma in the shadows of stumps on day three in Cape Town.

entries1.title: Triple-murderer Erin Patterson to learn her appeal fate today
entries1.summary: Victoria's Court of Appeal will announce its decision on the mushroom killer's bid to have her convictions overturned.

entries1.title: Spain begins three days of mourning as train crash death toll reaches 74
entries1.summary: Spain has begun three days of mourning after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 74 people.

entries1.title: Russell Brand's wife tells court actor's promiscuity left her 'heartbroken'
entries1.summary: Russell Brand is on trial in London charged with the rape, sexual assault and attempted indecent assault of six women between 1999 and 2009.

entries1.title: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian train platform kills 14
entries1.summary: A Russian drone has slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro killing at least 14 people.

entries1.title: Conflicting accounts emerge after Spanish train collision
entries1.summary: Contradictions have emerged between a private rail operator and the Spanish government over what caused Europe's deadliest train collision since 2013, according to local reports.

entries1.title: Child care sector faces further changes after shocking abuse exposed
entries1.summary: A proposed national childcare commission will be discussed at a meeting of education ministers next week, as the government faces renewed calls for changes following a Four Corners investigation into Australia's child care system.

entries1.title: North Korean workers sold into Russia then stripped of wages, report finds
entries1.summary: Russian brokers are advertising North Korean workers to companies as part of a forced labour program being used to fund Pyongyang's ballistic missile program, a new report has alleged.

entries1.title: Albanese is bogged down in grant problem of his own making
entries1.summary: Questions over a golf club grant were just the beginning of a tough week in parliament for Anthony Albanese and his government.

entries1.title: Alleged Haines attacker likely in state of psychosis, early prison report says
entries1.summary: An initial prison assessment of the man who allegedly attacked federal MP Helen Haines finds no indication of ideological extremism.

entries1.title: Inflation figures show it's going to get worse before it gets better
entries1.summary: The latest numbers cause pain for households, business and the government. They also show that a tougher approach may well be needed to curb the problem.

entries1.title: Australia records highest rates of anorexia and bulimia globally
entries1.summary: An international team of researchers has analysed global numbers of people with anorexia and bulimia nervosa, finding an increase of 71 per cent worldwide since 1990.

entries1.title: Teen in 'prime of her life' dies after drive-by shooting south of Brisbane
entries1.summary: Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, who was one of four people shot by two masked men during a boxing event at a Logan nightspot on Saturday night, died on Thursday at Princess Alexandra hospital.

entries1.title: Cigarette likely cause of catastrophic Hong Kong fire, report finds
entries1.summary: Hong Kong's chief executive announces the findings of a months-long investigation into the Wang Fuk Court apartment fire that killed 168 people last year.

entries1.title: Zacharia blames media for troubled stint as White House press secretary
entries1.summary: Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia has doubled down on support for Donald Trump.

entries1.title: NT teen faces terror charges as police seize 3D-printed gun schematics
entries1.summary: A teenage boy charged with serious terrorism and violent extremism offences after a raid in the NT is remanded in custody.

entries1.title: Relentless modern-day blitz as Russia rains jet-fuelled death on Ukrainians
entries1.summary: Moscow's new jet-powered drones rip through the sky at hundreds of kilometres an hour, slamming into buildings day and night, and Ukraine's defences are struggling to keep up.

entries1.title: WA Labor MP vows to 'vigorously defend' US lawsuit over $1m loan
entries1.summary: A Western Australian MP embroiled in a legal dispute over a million-dollar loan in the United States insists everything he did was above board.

entries1.title: Appeal challenges ruling on Sydney teacher's abuse of male students
entries1.summary: A challenge is underway in the Supreme Court after a judge ruled a former Sydney teacher who sexually abused male students in the 1970s could not have foreseen the harm she caused.

entries1.title: Actor's death may be first confirmed fatality linked to unapproved peptides
entries1.summary: A coroner has found the death of Australian actor Richard Norton was triggered by injecting unapproved peptides, recommending the TGA consider tougher restrictions.

entries1.title: Police search launched for man swept away in Central Australia flooding
entries1.summary: Police say a 60-year-old man is missing after he was reportedly swept off the roof of a vehicle that had "become stuck in floodwater" near Santa Teresa, with police now searching for him with drones and divers.

entries1.title: Businesses hoping for 'salvation' from Sydney's new metro line
entries1.summary: After two years of economic pain, the small businesses along Sydney's new Southwest Metro line are breathing a sigh of relief and hoping customers will return in droves.

entries1.title: SF TD signed off on two non-charity entities, court told

entries1.title: Former principal, 91, jailed over 'brazen' abuse of pupil
entries1.summary: A former principal of De La Salle National School in Waterford city has been sentenced to four years and three months in prison for abusing a child, with the final year suspended.

entries1.summary: The Democratic Unionist Party is to end joint engagements of Stormont's First Ministers' office in a row with Sinn Féin over Drumcree, a move Michelle O'Neill called "arrogant and supremacist".

entries1.summary: The death toll from the crash involving two high-speed trains in Spain has risen to 74 from 69, according to the transport ministry.

entries1.summary: Criminals are selling drug debts on to other groups who enforce what is allegedly owed at a higher amount, the Garda Commissioner has said.

entries1.summary: Arab parties in Israel have rejected accusations of foreign funding and accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of trying to scare the opposition against dealing with Israeli Arab politicians.

entries1.summary: Enoch Burke has been banned from going within 100 metres of a school in Co Westmeath after a judge amended an order against him.

entries1.summary: U2 have reassured fans at home that they will be announcing Irish shows as they unveiled UK and European dates for their upcoming tour, Carnaval de Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth.

entries1.summary: A suspected data breach is being investigated involving the Employment Permit Online System operated by the Department of Enterprise.

entries1.summary: The Government is planning to repay €8 billion in loans received during the financial crisis ahead of schedule.

entries1.title: Prison service proposed sentence cuts due to overcrowding
entries1.summary: Irish jails were so overcrowded that a proposal to cut 40 days from the sentence of every prisoner in the State was put forward by authorities struggling to find more space.

entries1.summary: Niamh Gallagher and Aoibheann Reilly have both been handed starts for Ireland's final WXV Global Series game of the season.

entries1.summary: The Chief of Staff of the Irish Defence Forces has said updated definitions of acceptable and unacceptable behaviour across the organisation have become part of its training, briefings and regulations.

entries1.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced her resignation today, ending months of speculation about her future just as Europe enters a period of rising economic volatility and divisive electoral politics.

entries1.title: Third quarter new home completions up by 10% - CSO
entries1.summary: There was a 10.4% increase in the number of new homes built in the third quarter of this year, from July to September, as 10,154 dwellings were finished.

entries1.summary: The Social Democrats have called for a public register of data centres to track their locations, carbon emissions, energy requirements and water usage.

entries1.summary: Russell Brand's wife has told his rape trial her husband is "caring" and "kind" and there is honesty at the centre of their marriage.

entries1.summary: Ireland has the capabilities to protect European leaders who will gather in Dublin for two major summits next month, the Tánaiste has said.

entries1.summary: A sea turtle, affectionately known as the 'queen of the shark tank' at Dingle Aquarium, has been released back into the sea after living at the aquarium for the past 22 years.

entries1.summary: Polling shows that Democrat James Talarico is neck-and-neck with Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, writes Jackie Fox.

entries1.summary: Just over a quarter of the population have experienced sexual violence as an adult, according to a report.

entries1.summary: All-Ireland SFC champions Mayo have secured six places on this year's PwC Football All-Star team, with eight different counties represented on the selection.

entries1.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris has rejected the "characterisation" of his phone call with Patrick O'Donovan hours before the media minister became ill at an EU event.

entries1.summary: A high-profile, anti-immigration campaigner has been cleared of a charge of making a false claim that an asylum seeker exposed himself on a bus to a teenage girl.

entries1.summary: US officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action against Iran after next week's US midterm elections.

entries1.summary: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as European Central Bank president ends an eventful seven years at an institution she was never expected to lead.

entries1.summary: EU energy ministers will meet to discuss energy security ahead of winter as the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Yemen send oil and natural gas prices soaring.

entries1.summary: A new initiative is required to challenge all traditions to engage with "hard evidence" on different constitutional frameworks around unity, the Taoiseach has said.

entries1.summary: The controversial bill to remove the triple lock from Irish law will not be debated by an Oireachtas committee until at least the second half of November.

entries1.summary: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has insisted that he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile.

entries1.summary: A verdict of death by misadventure has been recorded into the death of a man who became unresponsive after being held in a prone position by gardaí.

entries1.summary: President Vladimir Putin has hailed Elon Musk as a genius, acknowledging Russia is only beginning to roll out its answer to his Starlink satellite internet system.

entries2.title: Turtle returns to sea after 22 years at Kerry aquarium
entries2.summary: A sea turtle, affectionately known as the 'queen of the shark tank' at Dingle Aquarium, has been released back into the sea after living at the aquarium for the past 22 years.

entries2.title: Is the Republican stronghold of Texas turning blue?
entries2.summary: Polling shows that Democrat James Talarico is neck-and-neck with Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, writes Jackie Fox.

entries2.title: 26% of adults have experienced sexual violence - report
entries2.summary: Just over a quarter of the population have experienced sexual violence as an adult, according to a report.

entries2.title: McDonald among Mayo's All-Stars after dream summer
entries2.summary: All-Ireland SFC champions Mayo have secured six places on this year's PwC Football All-Star team, with eight different counties represented on the selection.

entries2.title: Harris rejects 'characterisation' of call with O'Donovan
entries2.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris has rejected the "characterisation" of his phone call with Patrick O'Donovan hours before the media minister became ill at an EU event.

entries2.title: Anti-immigration campaigner cleared of false claim charge
entries2.summary: A high-profile, anti-immigration campaigner has been cleared of a charge of making a false claim that an asylum seeker exposed himself on a bus to a teenage girl.

entries2.title: Irish eyes on Joanne McNally for Celeb Traitors reveal
entries2.summary: BBC One's The Celebrity Traitors will reveal tonight whether comedian Joanne McNally or actress Sharon Rooney will be banished after last week's cliffhanger left their fates hanging in the balance.

entries2.title: US warns allies of potential Iran strikes after midterms
entries2.summary: US officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action against Iran after next week's US midterm elections.

entries2.title: Christine Lagarde: The outsider who led the ECB her way
entries2.summary: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as European Central Bank president ends an eventful seven years at an institution she was never expected to lead.

entries2.title: EU energy ministers to discuss soaring fuel prices
entries2.summary: EU energy ministers will meet to discuss energy security ahead of winter as the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Yemen send oil and natural gas prices soaring.

entries2.title: Kompany released from hospital after training collapse
entries2.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital following his collapse last week.

entries2.title: Restored nature hits record level, still off target - UN
entries2.summary: Countries are restoring about 252 million hectares of nature, a record level according to a United Nations report, but this still falls short of global 2030 targets.

entries2.title: Initiative needed to define Irish unity debate - Martin
entries2.summary: A new initiative is required to challenge all traditions to engage with "hard evidence" on different constitutional frameworks around unity, the Taoiseach has said.

entries2.title: Social worker tells murder trial of concern for pensioner
entries2.summary: A social worker has told a jury at the Central Criminal Court of her concern for Josephine 'Josie' Ray in the months before her murder at her home in Nenagh, Co Tipperary two years ago.

entries2.title: Govt says opposition want to 'slow-walk' triple lock bill
entries2.summary: The controversial bill to remove the triple lock from Irish law will not be debated by an Oireachtas committee until at least the second half of November.

entries2.title: Bolsonaro says he is Brazil's leader after fleeing to US
entries2.summary: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has insisted that he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile.

entries2.title: Israeli election 'stolen' by Arab parties, says Likud
entries2.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud accused Arab parties of having stolen the country's election, after partial results showed they could play a kingmaking role in forming a new government.

entries2.title: Inquest jury recommends garda restraint training
entries2.summary: A verdict of death by misadventure has been recorded into the death of a man who became unresponsive after being held in a prone position by gardaí.

entries2.title: Putin salutes Musk's 'genius' as Russia follows Starlink
entries2.summary: President Vladimir Putin has hailed Elon Musk as a genius, acknowledging Russia is only beginning to roll out its answer to his Starlink satellite internet system.

entries2.title: Vance contacted top Iran security official - US outlet
entries2.summary: US Vice President JD Vance has contacted Iran's security chief in a bid to revive peace talks that could head off a renewed American assault on the Islamic republic, the Wall Street Journal has reported.

entries2.title: NI secretary ban on Drumcree march lawful, court rules
entries2.summary: A Belfast court has ruled that the Northern Secretary made a lawful decision when he banned the Drumcree parade earlier this month.

entries2.title: Jury discharged in case of man accused of father's murder
entries2.summary: A jury has been discharged two weeks into the trial of a man accused of murdering his father at the apartment they shared in Dublin.

entries2.title: Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassing two journalists
entries2.summary: Far-right activist Tommy Robinson has been convicted of harassing two journalists and causing them to fear violence.

entries2.title: Harris denies 'heated' O'Donovan call on day he fell ill
entries2.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris has confirmed he spoke to Patrick O'Donovan on the phone shortly before the Minister for Culture fell ill and was taken to hospital.

entries2.title: Girl, 8, attacked by wolf in German wildlife park
entries2.summary: A young girl has been attacked by a wolf and badly injured in a German wildlife park, police said, adding that the eight-year-old was taken to hospital by rescue helicopter.

entries2.title: McClean and Derry City mutually agree to part ways
entries2.summary: James McClean's second spell at Derry City has come to an end after the player and the club mutually agreed to terminate his contract with immediate effect.

entries2.title: Hospital overcrowding highest recorded this year - INMO
entries2.summary: There has been a further rise in hospital overcrowding with 824 patients waiting for admission to a bed, according to the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation.

entries2.title: Stroke survivor saved after speaking 'gibberish' on call
entries2.summary: A man is urging people to be aware of the stroke symptoms after he was saved by a colleague who noticed he was speaking "complete gibberish" on a work call.

entries2.title: 68% of households within 2km of high-frequency bus stop
entries2.summary: New figures from the Central Statistics Office reveal that eight in ten households are located within two kilometres of a bus stop while almost seven in ten are near a high-frequency bus service.

entries2.title: UK budget pledges billions in household supports
entries2.summary: British finance minister John Healey has announced support to help households through the "global economic storms" with subsidies for energy bills and a freeze in fuel duty for drivers in the first budget plan of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government.

entries2.title: Brand tells court he was 'wrong' to use his fame for sex
entries2.summary: Russell Brand told jurors at his rape trial he has dedicated much of his life to "beyond reckless philandering and idiocy", and admitted he had been wrong to use his fame to get sex.

entries2.title: Man, 92, guilty of indecent assault on sisters in 1970s
entries2.summary: A 92-year-old Co Clare man who paid out €60,000 two years ago to two orphaned sisters has been found guilty of eight counts of indecent assault.

entries1.title: Brazil reduces fragmented native vegetation area by 43% over 38 years
entries1.summary:
The area of native vegetation fragmented by deforestation for land-use change in Brazil has decreased by 43 percent over 38 years, as per data from the Degradation module of MapBiomas, released this Thursday (Oct. 29).

Brazil went from 287 hectares of fragmented forest in 1986 to 163 hectares in 2024. These are patches of original forest surrounded by areas cleared for agriculture, pasture, or urban development.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Amazon records lowest deforestation level in 41 years.
  • Brazil’s Cerrado loses 13.9M hectares of riverbank vegetation.
  • Luxembourg joins Tropical Forest Forever Facility.
Even though the total fragmented area has decreased, these patches have become smaller while their number has increased. There were 2.35 million patches of native vegetation in 1986, rising to 3.41 million in 2024.

According to Dhemerson Conciani, a researcher at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute (Ipam), these small fragments hinder seed dispersal and animal movement, directly affecting the reproduction of native species living in these areas. Conciani is also the technical coordinator of the Degradation Group at MapBiomas.

“[This fragmentation] reduces gene flow [the transfer of genetic material] and increases the risk of local extinctions.”

Biomes

When the data are broken down by biome, the Atlantic forest is the most affected, with 1.38 million fragmented areas, and the cerrado ranks second, comprising 957,000 small patches of native vegetation.

The Atlantic forest also contains the smallest fragments, with an average area of 25 hectares. With an average area of 81 hectares, the pampa is the second-most fragmented biome, followed by the cerrado, where fragments average 105 hectares.

In the Amazon, although the fragments will be the largest in terms of area by 2024 – at 662 hectares – their size has decreased by 76 percent since 1986, when the average fragment size was 2,700 hectares.

The number of isolated fragments separated by deforested areas has also increased over 38 years, rising from 144,000 fragments in 1986 to 519,000 in 2024 – a 260 percent surge.

“The more fragmented the landscape becomes, the smaller the average area of its fragments, and this is terrible in environmental terms because it drastically increases exposure to edge effects and fire, especially in years with extreme weather events,” Conciani stated.

Vulnerability

Edge areas are strips of land adjacent (30 to 150 meters) to deforested regions that suffer the effects of degradation because they are subjected to conditions different from those in preserved areas – such as excessive sunlight, vulnerability to strong winds, and soil siltation due to moisture loss.

According to researchers, 37 million to 102 million hectares of native vegetation are located in these edge zones across Brazil. This represents 7 to 18 percent of the country’s native vegetation.

Among the Brazilian biomes, the cerrado has the largest area of native vegetation exposed to the vulnerabilities of edge zones. It spans 11 million to 32 million hectares. In terms of proportion, however, the Atlantic forest is the most exposed biome, with 29 to 66 percent of its total remaining native vegetation located in edge zones.

COP17

The study was presented this Thursday (29) in Yerevan, Armenia, during the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

According to GeoKarten researcher Eduardo Vélez, who is also a member of the MapBiomas Degradation Group, understanding the dynamics of native vegetation loss and fragmentation is key to addressing the global biodiversity crisis.

“The previously unpublished and updated information on the fragmentation of native vegetation in Brazil is crucial for understanding the scale of the problem, preventing it from worsening, and even guiding restoration efforts aimed at achieving greater ecological connectivity.”

entries1.title: Flávio’s campaign coordinator: No evidence of election fraud
entries1.summary:
Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), the Senate opposition leader and Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign coordinator, commented on the candidate’s release of a letter described as coup-mongering. Flávio fled to the US with his family after losing the presidential election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

In an initial version of the letter, posted on X on Wednesday (Oct. 28), Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the original post was deleted and replaced with a revised version that changed “president-elect” to “leader of Brazil.”

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid.
  • On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
“The letter posted on his Twitter [X] account - which is an official letter, the definitive version - presents him as a leader. In fact, given the number of votes he received and the role he played in the last election, Flávio is now the leading figure of the right in Brazil,” Marinho said at a press conference in the Senate. “I believe there must have been some problem with the drafting of the letter,” he added, referring to the change in wording.

When asked whether there had been fraud in Brazil’s election - a claim Flávio Bolsonaro makes without providing evidence in the letter - Rogério Marinho acknowledged that he had no evidence to support it.

“The PL cannot make that claim, nor can I, because there is no evidence to support it,” he acknowledged.

Marinho described Flávio Bolsonaro’s accusation in the letter as an emotional outburst following his decision to leave the country. He also referred to Flávio Bolsonaro as an “exile,” although the senator left Brazil voluntarily and without an arrest warrant.

entries1.title: Former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro charged in fraud case
entries1.summary:
On Wednesday (Oct. 28), Brazil’s Federal Police charged former banker Daniel Vorcaro and 14 others under investigation for financial fraud at the state-owned Banco Regional de Brasília (BRB). The irregularities were brought under scrutiny during the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero.

The police report states that Vorcaro played a “personal, repeated, and directive role” in transactions involving irregular loan portfolios at Banco Master that caused losses to BRB.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Top court to rule if Justice Moraes can be probed in bank fraud case.
  • Lula urges full disclosure on Brazil’s “biggest financial crime”.
  • Billions frozen in crackdown on Brazil’s biggest bank fraud case.
“As the controlling shareholder of Banco Master, Vorcaro stood at the center of decision-making within the framework under investigation and was the primary economic beneficiary of the transactions intended to secure liquidity for the institution,” the Federal Police concluded.

He was arrested in March this year and is being held at the Papudinha prison in the Federal District.

In addition to Vorcaro, the list of those charged also includes former BRB President Paulo Henrique Costa and Augusto Lima, a former partner at Master.

All those under investigation have been charged with fraudulent management of a financial institution, criminal organization, and money laundering.

Losses

According to the federal investigators, the losses already determined amount to some BRL 2.7 billion. Part of the losses was caused by nonexistent loan portfolios held in the name of Tirreno, a shell company operated by Master, which conducted transactions with BRB.

“There are, therefore, some BRL 2.7 billion in losses that have already been formally documented and acknowledged. This is not an abstract estimate or a merely contingent risk,” the Federal Police stated.

After concluding the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero, investigators submitted the report to Brazil’s prosecutor-general and requested that the Supreme Court extend the probes for an additional 60 days.

The extension will be used to complete the pending forensic examinations and to submit a supplementary investigative report.

In a statement, Daniel Vorcaro’s defense team denied that BRB’s transactions with Tirreno caused any losses to the state-owned bank.

According to the lawyers, “the deal involving Tirreno’s portfolios was not finalized. The portfolios were replaced by other assets, and the exchange that took place demonstrates that the transactions between Banco Master and BRB generated positive results for Banco de Brasília. No official forensic investigation has found any loss,” the defense stated.

entries1.title: Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid
entries1.summary:
After fleeing Brazil for the United States, defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter thanking Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump for their support in helping him escape the country.

In an initial version of the coup-mongering letter, the senator declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the wording was changed to “leader of Brazil.”

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
In the letter, the defeated candidate alleges, without providing evidence, that Brazil’s election was rigged. He also criticizes Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting hours until 7 p.m., following a request from the campaigns of both the Liberal Party and the Workers’ Party.

Flávio Bolsonaro was defeated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential runoff held last Sunday (Oct. 25), with Lula receiving 64 million votes. Flávio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, received just over 59 million votes. The two-hour extension of voting hours accounted for only 34,393 votes. According to the Superior Electoral Court, approximately 158.7 million Brazilian voters were eligible to vote.

“A decision by the Superior Electoral Court, which overstepped its authority, extended voting at the eleventh hour. The order arrived only after the legal voting hours had ended and the polls had already closed,” Flávio Bolsonaro complained.

His claims contradict the Superior Electoral Court’s official vote count and certification of the election. The outcome was also recognized by the Organization of American States (OAS) and leaders from countries across several continents. Flávio Bolsonaro’s own party, the Liberal Party (PL), also acknowledged Lula’s victory.

In the letter, Flávio Bolsonaro also criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’s decision to bar him from leaving the country and order the seizure of his personal and diplomatic passports. Moraes issued the order at the request of the Federal Police, which cited the risk that the senator might flee amid investigations into alleged money laundering and currency evasion.

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation in two cases before the Supreme Court. In one, he and attorney Willer Tomaz are suspected of money laundering through betting platforms. He is also under investigation over the financing of Dark Horse, a film about his father’s career.

In a statement released by his press office, he said he would lead the opposition from the US.

Escape

The senator arrived in Miami, Florida, with his wife and two daughters on Wednesday morning (28), following a day of uncertainty about his whereabouts. The family crossed into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil, with Puerto Iguazú, Argentina. At 11:30 p.m., they boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador, before continuing on to the US.

Democrats

On Wednesday morning (28), the US House Foreign Affairs Committee criticized the Trump administration for granting a visa to Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

On social media, the committee, which is aligned with the Democratic Party, contrasted current US immigration policies toward people fleeing conflict with the treatment of Flávio Bolsonaro and his family.

“No asylum for people fleeing the war in Sudan or conflicts in Haiti, but [Secretary of State Marco] Rubio is rolling out the red carpet for Bolsonaro,” the committee said in a post on X.

entries1.title: On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”
entries1.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (Oct. 28) that he “will not get involved” when asked about a coup-mongering letter released by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in which he declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the senator changed the wording to “leader of Brazil.”

Trump confirmed that the US had granted visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and once again questioned the integrity of Brazil’s electoral process without providing evidence.

“I’m not going to comment on that, but I know we gave him authorization to enter the country. I’m not going to get involved. It was a very strange election, that’s for sure,” Trump said.

entries1.title: Lula terms Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape “shameful”
entries1.summary:
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Tuesday (Oct. 27) described Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape to the US as “shameful.” In the opinion of the president, who was reelected last Sunday (Oct. 25), his opponent at the polls is in debt to the justice system.

“A citizen who secretly flees his country does so because he must have something to hide,” said Lula.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Aircraft carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family lands in US.
“This act of leaving Brazil is shameful. He should have turned in his passport. The Federal Police must have already suspected he would leave Brazil – he is under investigation,” he added.

Lula welcomed supporters who had gathered to celebrate his 81st birthday outside the Alvorada Palace, the president’s official residence. There, he cut a cake and gave a speech.

The president recalled the time he himself was arrested in April 2018, when he handed over his passport and turned himself in to the Federal Police.

“I decided to turn myself in to the Federal Police because I wanted to expose my accusers and prove my innocence,” he said. At the time, Lula spent 580 days in prison and was released on November 8, 2019.

“And here I am, being reelected for another term thanks to you. That’s why I tell you, those who have done nothing wrong have nothing to fear,” Lula added.

In 2021, Brazil’s Supreme Court overturned the cases handled by former Judge Sergio Moro, recognizing that he had been biased in the investigation involving Lula. Today, Moro is the governor-elect for the Liberal Party – or PL – the party of Flávio Bolsonaro, with whom he is allied.

entries1.summary:
The aircraft that departed Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, for Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board is currently en route to Miami International Airport in the US.
