entries1.title: Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape
entries1.summary:
Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, told the press on Tuesday (Oct. 27) that he was unaware of Flávio and his family’s departure for the US.

“We are surprised because yesterday we discussed the need for Flávio - with the 60 million votes he received - to take on a leadership role in the opposition, which is important because, in our assessment, we have a government that has clearly been harmful to the country,” said Marinho after attending a meeting with lawmakers and political leaders from the PL in Brasília.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro’s party acknowledges Lula’s victory.
Marinho also mentioned that he had received a text message from Flávio Bolsonaro around 8 a.m. on Tuesday (27), in which he said he was going to “take some time off” and would later speak with his allies again.

The undisclosed trip to the US, whose details remain unknown, took place less than 48 hours after he lost the presidential election to Lula. The move was reported by Reuters and confirmed by a US government official.

Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, including Senator-elect Carlos Jordy (PL – Rio de Janeiro), have issued statements confirming his departure.

“Confirmed! Flávio Bolsonaro went to the US to avoid being used as a bargaining chip in efforts to impeach Moraes!” said Jordy, referring to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

Despite this, no official from Brazil or the US has made a public statement about his departure.

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation by the Federal Police in several cases involving alleged crimes such as currency evasion, money laundering, and corruption. His term as senator for Rio de Janeiro ends in February 2027, when he will lose his special jurisdiction.

Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered on Monday (26) that the former candidate surrender his passports to the police; however, the documents were not handed over.

The court order is part of the case in which Flávio Bolsonaro and attorney Willer Tomaz are being investigated by the Supreme Court for money laundering.

Due to his failure to comply with the order, the Federal Police revoked the senator’s passports.

In a video posted on Monday, Flávio denied that he had plans to leave the country and said he would turn in his passports.

Agência Brasil contacted Flávio Bolsonaro’s press office but received no response.

entries1.title: Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador
entries1.summary:
Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party), his wife, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and their two daughters, Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro, entered Argentina on Tuesday night (Oct. 27). The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

entries2.title: Brazil reduces fragmented native vegetation area by 43% over 38 years
entries2.summary:
The area of native vegetation fragmented by deforestation for land-use change in Brazil has decreased by 43 percent over 38 years, as per data from the Degradation module of MapBiomas, released this Thursday (Oct. 29).

Brazil went from 287 hectares of fragmented forest in 1986 to 163 hectares in 2024. These are patches of original forest surrounded by areas cleared for agriculture, pasture, or urban development.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Amazon records lowest deforestation level in 41 years.
  • Brazil’s Cerrado loses 13.9M hectares of riverbank vegetation.
  • Luxembourg joins Tropical Forest Forever Facility.
Even though the total fragmented area has decreased, these patches have become smaller while their number has increased. There were 2.35 million patches of native vegetation in 1986, rising to 3.41 million in 2024.

According to Dhemerson Conciani, a researcher at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute (Ipam), these small fragments hinder seed dispersal and animal movement, directly affecting the reproduction of native species living in these areas. Conciani is also the technical coordinator of the Degradation Group at MapBiomas.

“[This fragmentation] reduces gene flow [the transfer of genetic material] and increases the risk of local extinctions.”

Biomes

When the data are broken down by biome, the Atlantic forest is the most affected, with 1.38 million fragmented areas, and the cerrado ranks second, comprising 957,000 small patches of native vegetation.

The Atlantic forest also contains the smallest fragments, with an average area of 25 hectares. With an average area of 81 hectares, the pampa is the second-most fragmented biome, followed by the cerrado, where fragments average 105 hectares.

In the Amazon, although the fragments will be the largest in terms of area by 2024 – at 662 hectares – their size has decreased by 76 percent since 1986, when the average fragment size was 2,700 hectares.

The number of isolated fragments separated by deforested areas has also increased over 38 years, rising from 144,000 fragments in 1986 to 519,000 in 2024 – a 260 percent surge.

“The more fragmented the landscape becomes, the smaller the average area of its fragments, and this is terrible in environmental terms because it drastically increases exposure to edge effects and fire, especially in years with extreme weather events,” Conciani stated.

Vulnerability

Edge areas are strips of land adjacent (30 to 150 meters) to deforested regions that suffer the effects of degradation because they are subjected to conditions different from those in preserved areas – such as excessive sunlight, vulnerability to strong winds, and soil siltation due to moisture loss.

According to researchers, 37 million to 102 million hectares of native vegetation are located in these edge zones across Brazil. This represents 7 to 18 percent of the country’s native vegetation.

Among the Brazilian biomes, the cerrado has the largest area of native vegetation exposed to the vulnerabilities of edge zones. It spans 11 million to 32 million hectares. In terms of proportion, however, the Atlantic forest is the most exposed biome, with 29 to 66 percent of its total remaining native vegetation located in edge zones.

COP17

The study was presented this Thursday (29) in Yerevan, Armenia, during the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

According to GeoKarten researcher Eduardo Vélez, who is also a member of the MapBiomas Degradation Group, understanding the dynamics of native vegetation loss and fragmentation is key to addressing the global biodiversity crisis.

“The previously unpublished and updated information on the fragmentation of native vegetation in Brazil is crucial for understanding the scale of the problem, preventing it from worsening, and even guiding restoration efforts aimed at achieving greater ecological connectivity.”

The plane that departed from Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, representing Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board landed shortly before 10:30 a.m. Brasília time on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at Opa-Locka Airport in Miami, US.

According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the trip lasted about four hours.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
Flávio, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones.

At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

entries2.title: Plane carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family heads to Miami
entries2.summary:
The aircraft that departed Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, for Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board is currently en route to Miami International Airport in the US. According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the plane should land on US soil around 10:20 a.m. Brasília time.

Flávio Bolsonaro, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (Oct. 27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
On Tuesday, a close ally of Flávio Bolsonaro and a US government source confirmed to Reuters that the senator had fled to the US. Flávio failed to meet the deadline set by Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Court to surrender his passports to the Federal Police.

The day before, in a video posted on social media after being summoned by the judiciary, Flávio had denied any intention of leaving Brazil and said he would remain in the country to, as he put it, organize opposition to the government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was reelected on Sunday (26) after defeating the senator in the second round of the presidential election.

entries2.title: Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape
entries2.summary:
Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, told the press on Tuesday (Oct. 27) that he was unaware of Flávio and his family’s departure for the US.

“We are surprised because yesterday we discussed the need for Flávio - with the 60 million votes he received - to take on a leadership role in the opposition, which is important because, in our assessment, we have a government that has clearly been harmful to the country,” said Marinho after attending a meeting with lawmakers and political leaders from the PL in Brasília.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro’s party acknowledges Lula’s victory.
Marinho also mentioned that he had received a text message from Flávio Bolsonaro around 8 a.m. on Tuesday (27), in which he said he was going to “take some time off” and would later speak with his allies again.

The undisclosed trip to the US, whose details remain unknown, took place less than 48 hours after he lost the presidential election to Lula. The move was reported by Reuters and confirmed by a US government official.

Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, including Senator-elect Carlos Jordy (PL – Rio de Janeiro), have issued statements confirming his departure.

“Confirmed! Flávio Bolsonaro went to the US to avoid being used as a bargaining chip in efforts to impeach Moraes!” said Jordy, referring to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

Despite this, no official from Brazil or the US has made a public statement about his departure.

Investigations

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation by the Federal Police in several cases involving alleged crimes such as currency evasion, money laundering, and corruption. His term as senator for Rio de Janeiro ends in February 2027, when he will lose his special jurisdiction.

Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered on Monday (26) that the former candidate surrender his passports to the police; however, the documents were not handed over.

The court order is part of the case in which Flávio Bolsonaro and attorney Willer Tomaz are being investigated by the Supreme Court for money laundering.

Due to his failure to comply with the order, the Federal Police revoked the senator’s passports.

In a video posted on Monday, Flávio denied that he had plans to leave the country and said he would turn in his passports.

Agência Brasil contacted Flávio Bolsonaro’s press office but received no response.

entries2.title: Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador
entries2.summary:
Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party), his wife, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and their two daughters, Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro, entered Argentina on Tuesday night (Oct. 27). The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

In a statement, the agency specified that they crossed the border at 10:50 p.m. via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., according to the Argentine government, Flávio and his family boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly and flew to Guayaquil, Ecuador, as indicated in the flight plan.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro rejects Lula’s victory, seeks to annul election.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
Also, Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration stated that the four presented valid travel documents and faced no legal impediment to entering the country. “The crossing was recorded by immigration authorities without incident,” the agency reported.

    <title>Brazil reduces fragmented native vegetation area by 43% over 38 years</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/meio-ambiente/noticia/2026-10/brazil-reduces-fragmented-native-vegetation-area-43-over-38-years</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/e3EMsi1N1mtM-kFcQd49yv8sb1M=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/mataatlanciaempe28093.jpg?itok=_FCXaFw2</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/meio-ambiente/noticia/2026-10/brazil-reduces-fragmented-native-vegetation-area-43-over-38-years">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p>The area of native vegetation fragmented by deforestation for land-use change in Brazil has decreased by 43 percent over 38 years, as per data from the Degradation module of MapBiomas, released this Thursday (Oct. 29).<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707220&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707220&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>Brazil went from 287 hectares of fragmented forest in 1986 to 163 hectares in 2024.<strong> These are patches of original forest surrounded by areas cleared for agriculture, pasture, or urban development.</strong></p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/meio-ambiente/noticia/2026-10/amazon-records-lowest-deforestation-level-41-years">Amazon records lowest deforestation level in 41 years.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/meio-ambiente/noticia/2026-10/brazils-cerrado-loses-139m-hectares-riverbank-vegetation">Brazil’s Cerrado loses 13.9M hectares of riverbank vegetation.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-06/luxembourg-joins-tropical-forest-forever-facility">Luxembourg joins Tropical Forest Forever Facility.</a></li></ul>Even though the total fragmented area has decreased, these patches have become smaller while <strong>their number has increased.</strong> There were 2.35 million patches of native vegetation in 1986, rising to 3.41 million in 2024.</p>

<p>According to Dhemerson Conciani, a researcher at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute (Ipam), <strong>these small fragments hinder seed dispersal and animal movement, directly affecting the reproduction of native species living in these areas.</strong> Conciani is also the technical coordinator of the Degradation Group at MapBiomas.</p>

<p>“[This fragmentation] reduces gene flow [the transfer of genetic material] and increases the risk of local extinctions.”</p>

<h2>Biomes</h2>

<p>When the data are broken down by biome, the <strong>Atlantic forest</strong> is the most affected, with 1.38 million fragmented areas, and the <strong>cerrado</strong> ranks second, comprising 957,000 small patches of native vegetation.</p>

<p>The Atlantic forest also contains the smallest fragments, with an average area of 25 hectares. With an average area of 81 hectares, the <strong>pampa</strong> is the second-most fragmented biome, followed by the cerrado, where fragments average 105 hectares.</p>

<p>In the <strong>Amazon</strong>, although the fragments will be the largest in terms of area by 2024 – at 662 hectares – their size has decreased by 76 percent since 1986, when the average fragment size was 2,700 hectares.</p>

<p>The number of isolated fragments separated by deforested areas has also increased over 38 years, rising from 144,000 fragments in 1986 to 519,000 in 2024 – a 260 percent surge.</p>

<p>“The more fragmented the landscape becomes, the smaller the average area of its fragments, and <strong>this is terrible in environmental terms because it drastically increases exposure to edge effects and fire, especially in years with extreme weather events</strong>,” Conciani stated.</p>

<h2>Vulnerability</h2>

<p>Edge areas are strips of land adjacent (30 to 150 meters) to deforested regions that suffer the effects of degradation because they are subjected to conditions different from those in preserved areas – such as excessive sunlight, vulnerability to strong winds, and soil siltation due to moisture loss.</p>

<p>According to researchers, 37 million to 102 million hectares of native vegetation are located in these edge zones across Brazil. This represents 7 to 18 percent of the country’s native vegetation.</p>

<p>Among the Brazilian biomes, the cerrado has the largest area of native vegetation exposed to the vulnerabilities of edge zones. It spans 11 million to 32 million hectares. In terms of proportion, however, the Atlantic forest is the most exposed biome, with 29 to 66 percent of its total remaining native vegetation located in edge zones.</p>

<h2>COP17</h2>

<p>The study was presented this Thursday (29) in Yerevan, Armenia, during the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).</p>

<p>According to GeoKarten researcher Eduardo Vélez, who is also a member of the MapBiomas Degradation Group, <strong>understanding the dynamics of native vegetation loss and fragmentation is key to addressing the global biodiversity crisis.</strong></p>

<p>“The previously unpublished and updated information on the fragmentation of native vegetation in Brazil is crucial for understanding the scale of the problem, preventing it from worsening, and even guiding restoration efforts aimed at achieving greater ecological connectivity.”</p>
</description>

    <title>Flávio’s campaign coordinator: No evidence of election fraud</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavios-campaign-coordinator-no-evidence-election-fraud</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/KuSc9BBVUm9X_uO_gCEs4xdLHOQ=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/rogerio_marinho_ministro_do_desenvolvimento_regional_jfcrz_abr_2012215424.jpg?itok=SKGQnc8i</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavios-campaign-coordinator-no-evidence-election-fraud">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p><strong>Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), the Senate opposition leader and Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign coordinator, commented on the candidate’s release of a letter described as coup-mongering. </strong>Flávio fled to the US with his family after losing the presidential election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707203&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707203&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>In an initial version of the letter, posted on X on Wednesday (Oct. 28), Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the original post was deleted and replaced with a revised version that changed “president-elect” to “leader of Brazil.”</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-thanks-trump-milei-aid-coup-mongering-letter">Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/trump-says-he-will-not-get-involved-after-flavio-bolsonaros-letter">On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/campaign-coordinator-says-he-was-surprised-flavios-escape">Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.</a></li></ul>“The letter posted on his Twitter [X] account - which is an official letter, the definitive version - presents him as a leader. In fact, given the number of votes he received and the role he played in the last election, Flávio is now the leading figure of the right in Brazil,” Marinho said at a press conference in the Senate. “I believe there must have been some problem with the drafting of the letter,” he added, referring to the change in wording.</p>

<p>When asked whether there had been fraud in Brazil’s election - a claim Flávio Bolsonaro makes without providing evidence in the letter - Rogério Marinho acknowledged that he had no evidence to support it.</p>

<p>“The PL cannot make that claim, nor can I, because there is no evidence to support it,” he acknowledged.</p>

<p><strong>Marinho described Flávio Bolsonaro’s accusation in the letter as an emotional outburst following his decision to leave the country. He also referred to Flávio Bolsonaro as an “exile,” although the senator left Brazil voluntarily and without an arrest warrant.</strong></p>

<p><strong>He is under investigation in several cases involving alleged money laundering, currency evasion, and corruption.</strong></p>

<p>In one of these cases, he is suspected of money laundering through betting platforms alongside attorney Willer Tomaz. He is also the subject of an investigation into the financing of <em>Dark Horse</em>, a film chronicling his father’s career. Starting next year, his Senate term will come to an end, and he will lose his privileged jurisdiction and parliamentary immunity.</p>

<p>Rogério Marinho also commented on US President Donald Trump’s statement that he “will not get involved” in the controversy surrounding Flávio Bolsonaro’s coup-mongering letter. The allied senator said Trump has the right to express his views on international politics but stressed that Brazil must resolve its own problems, rejecting foreign intervention.</p>

<p>“I hope there will be no intervention in Brazil’s internal affairs,” Marinho added.</p>
</description>

    <title>Former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro charged in fraud case</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/justica/noticia/2026-10/former-banco-master-owner-daniel-vorcaro-charged-fraud-case</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/HN9FF1bKJbokttMbBg1AgDE6hyY=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/03/06/daniel_vorcaro.jpg?itok=uJbwWRip</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/justica/noticia/2026-10/former-banco-master-owner-daniel-vorcaro-charged-fraud-case">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p>On Wednesday (Oct. 28), Brazil’s Federal Police charged former banker Daniel Vorcaro and 14 others under investigation for financial fraud at the state-owned Banco Regional de Brasília (BRB). The irregularities were brought under scrutiny during the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707171&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707171&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>The police report states that <strong>Vorcaro played a “personal, repeated, and directive role” in transactions involving irregular loan portfolios at Banco Master that caused losses to BRB.</strong></p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/justica/noticia/2026-09/top-court-rule-if-justice-moraes-can-be-probed-bank-fraud-case">Top court to rule if Justice Moraes can be probed in bank fraud case.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-09/lula-urges-full-disclosure-brazils-biggest-financial-crime">Lula urges full disclosure on Brazil’s “biggest financial crime”.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/justica/noticia/2026-05/billions-frozen-crackdown-brazils-biggest-bank-fraud-case">Billions frozen in crackdown on Brazil’s biggest bank fraud case.</a></li></ul>“As the controlling shareholder of Banco Master, Vorcaro stood at the center of decision-making within the framework under investigation and was the primary economic beneficiary of the transactions intended to secure liquidity for the institution,” the Federal Police concluded.</p>

<p><strong>He was arrested in March this year</strong> and is being held at the Papudinha prison in the Federal District.</p>

<p>In addition to Vorcaro, <strong>the list of those charged also includes former BRB President Paulo Henrique Costa and Augusto Lima, a former partner at Master.</strong></p>

<p>All those under investigation have been charged with <strong>fraudulent management of a financial institution, criminal organization, and money laundering.</strong></p>

<h2>Losses</h2>

<p>According to the federal investigators, the losses already determined amount to some BRL 2.7 billion. Part of the losses was caused by nonexistent loan portfolios held in the name of Tirreno, a shell company operated by Master, which conducted transactions with BRB.</p>

<p>“There are, therefore, some BRL 2.7 billion in losses that have already been formally documented and acknowledged. This is not an abstract estimate or a merely contingent risk,” the Federal Police stated.</p>

<p>After concluding the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero, <strong>investigators submitted the report to Brazil’s prosecutor-general and requested that the Supreme Court extend the probes for an additional 60 days.</strong></p>

<p>The extension will be used to complete the pending forensic examinations and to submit a supplementary investigative report.</p>

<h2>The Other Side</h2>

<p>In a statement, Daniel Vorcaro’s <strong>defense team denied that BRB’s transactions with Tirreno caused any losses</strong> to the state-owned bank.</p>

<p>According to the lawyers, “the deal involving Tirreno’s portfolios was not finalized. The portfolios were replaced by other assets, and the exchange that took place demonstrates that the transactions between Banco Master and BRB generated positive results for Banco de Brasília. No official forensic investigation has found any loss,” the defense stated.</p>
</description>

    <title>Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-thanks-trump-milei-aid-coup-mongering-letter</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/sKPd4d8UKTn0AdJBba5m8qn_d50=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/25/0d4a6236.jpg?itok=3AF9OK3O</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-thanks-trump-milei-aid-coup-mongering-letter">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p><strong>After fleeing Brazil for the United States, defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter thanking Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump for their support in helping him escape the country.</strong><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707166&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707166&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>In an initial version of the coup-mongering letter, the senator declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the wording was changed to “leader of Brazil.”</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador">Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/campaign-coordinator-says-he-was-surprised-flavios-escape">Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li></ul>In the letter, the defeated candidate alleges, without providing evidence, that Brazil’s election was rigged. He also criticizes Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting hours until 7 p.m., following a request from the campaigns of both the Liberal Party and the Workers’ Party.</p>

<p><strong>Flávio Bolsonaro was defeated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential runoff held last Sunday (Oct. 25), with Lula receiving 64 million votes. Flávio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, received just over 59 million votes.</strong> The two-hour extension of voting hours accounted for only 34,393 votes. According to the Superior Electoral Court, approximately 158.7 million Brazilian voters were eligible to vote.</p>

<p>“A decision by the Superior Electoral Court, which overstepped its authority, extended voting at the eleventh hour. The order arrived only after the legal voting hours had ended and the polls had already closed,” Flávio Bolsonaro complained.</p>

<p>His claims contradict the Superior Electoral Court’s official vote count and certification of the election. The outcome was also recognized by the Organization of American States (OAS) and leaders from countries across several continents. Flávio Bolsonaro’s own party, the Liberal Party (PL), also acknowledged Lula’s victory.</p>

<p>In the letter, Flávio Bolsonaro also criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’s decision to bar him from leaving the country and order the seizure of his personal and diplomatic passports. Moraes issued the order at the request of the Federal Police, which cited the risk that the senator might flee amid investigations into alleged money laundering and currency evasion.</p>

<p><strong>Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation in two cases before the Supreme Court.</strong> In one, he and attorney Willer Tomaz are suspected of money laundering through betting platforms. He is also under investigation over the financing of <em>Dark Horse</em>, a film about his father’s career.</p>

<p>In a statement released by his press office, he said he would lead the opposition from the US.</p>

<h2>Escape</h2>

<p>The senator arrived in Miami, Florida, with his wife and two daughters on Wednesday morning (28), following a day of uncertainty about his whereabouts. The family crossed into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil, with Puerto Iguazú, Argentina. At 11:30 p.m., they boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador, before continuing on to the US.</p>

<h2>Democrats</h2>

<p><strong>On Wednesday morning (28), the US House Foreign Affairs Committee criticized the Trump administration for granting a visa to Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.</strong></p>

<p>On social media, the committee, which is aligned with the Democratic Party, contrasted current US immigration policies toward people fleeing conflict with the treatment of Flávio Bolsonaro and his family.</p>

<p>“No asylum for people fleeing the war in Sudan or conflicts in Haiti, but [Secretary of State Marco] Rubio is rolling out the red carpet for Bolsonaro,” the committee said in a post on X.</p>
</description>

    <title>On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/trump-says-he-will-not-get-involved-after-flavio-bolsonaros-letter</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/aX4GQKcT4Ke0I0BRdrUfmIPAgNA=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/26/2026-10-26t221053z_2_lynxnpem9p1rv_rtroptp_4_usa-trump.jpg?itok=paPDwWJQ</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/trump-says-he-will-not-get-involved-after-flavio-bolsonaros-letter">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p><strong>US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (Oct. 28) that he “will not get involved” when asked about a coup-mongering letter released by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in which he declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.”</strong> Half an hour later, the senator changed the wording to “leader of Brazil.”<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707169&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707169&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>Trump confirmed that the US had granted visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and once again questioned the integrity of Brazil’s electoral process without providing evidence.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador">Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-rejects-lulas-victory-seeks-annul-election">Flávio Bolsonaro rejects Lula’s victory, seeks to annul election.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li></ul>“I’m not going to comment on that, but I know we gave him authorization to enter the country. I’m not going to get involved. It was a very strange election, that’s for sure,” Trump said.</p>

<p>Earlier, after fleeing Brazil for the United States, <strong>Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter thanking Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump for their support in helping him escape the country.</strong></p>

<p>In the document, the defeated candidate alleges, without providing evidence, that Brazil’s election was rigged. He also criticizes Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting hours until 7 p.m., following a request from the campaigns of the Liberal Party (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro’s party, and the Workers’ Party (PT), Lula’s party.</p>
</description>

    <title>Lula terms Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape “shameful”</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/lula-terms-flavio-bolsonaros-escape-shameful</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/A7sYQhrymbOQJwSSql6zHImnIRk=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/27/0d7a1712.jpg.jpeg?itok=yX9MgI_0</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/lula-terms-flavio-bolsonaros-escape-shameful">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p>President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Tuesday (Oct. 27) described Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape to the US as “shameful.” In the opinion of the president, who was reelected last Sunday (Oct. 25), his opponent at the polls is in debt to the justice system.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707071&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707071&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>“A citizen who secretly flees his country does so because he must have something to hide,” said Lula.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-fled-us-reuters-reports">Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/aircraft-carrying-flavio-bolsonaro-and-his-family-lands-us">Aircraft carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family lands in US.</a></li></ul>“<strong>This act of leaving Brazil is shameful. He should have turned in his passport. The Federal Police must have already suspected he would leave Brazil – he is under investigation,” </strong>he added.</p>

<p>Lula welcomed supporters who had gathered to celebrate his 81st birthday outside the Alvorada Palace, the president’s official residence. There, he cut a cake and gave a speech.</p>

<p><strong>The president recalled the time he himself was arrested</strong> in April 2018, when he handed over his passport and turned himself in to the Federal Police.</p>

<p>“I decided to turn myself in to the Federal Police because I wanted to expose my accusers and prove my innocence,” he said. At the time, Lula spent 580 days in prison and was released on November 8, 2019.</p>

<p>“And here I am, being reelected for another term thanks to you. That’s why I tell you, those who have done nothing wrong have nothing to fear,” Lula added.</p>

<p>In 2021, Brazil’s Supreme Court overturned the cases handled by former Judge Sergio Moro, recognizing that he had been biased in the investigation involving Lula. Today, Moro is the governor-elect for the Liberal Party – or PL – the party of Flávio Bolsonaro, with whom he is allied.</p>
</description>

    <title>Aircraft carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family lands in US</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/aircraft-carrying-flavio-bolsonaro-and-his-family-lands-us</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/vNJiw_5xA_BVIH9JKAt1Qc-QZIs=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/28/flavio_bolsonaro01.jpg?itok=lwHk747r</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/aircraft-carrying-flavio-bolsonaro-and-his-family-lands-us">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p>The plane that departed from Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, representing Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board landed shortly before 10:30 a.m. Brasília time on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at Opa-Locka Airport in Miami, US.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707050&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707050&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the trip lasted about four hours.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador">Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/campaign-coordinator-says-he-was-surprised-flavios-escape">Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.</a></li></ul>Flávio, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones.</p>

<p>At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.</p>
</description>

  <item>
    <title>Plane carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family heads to Miami</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/plane-carrying-flavio-bolsonaro-and-his-family-heads-miami</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/sKPd4d8UKTn0AdJBba5m8qn_d50=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/25/0d4a6236.jpg?itok=3AF9OK3O</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/plane-carrying-flavio-bolsonaro-and-his-family-heads-miami">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p>The aircraft that departed Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, for Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board is currently en route to Miami International Airport in the US. According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the plane should land on US soil around 10:20 a.m. Brasília time.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707041&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707041&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>Flávio Bolsonaro, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (Oct. 27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-fled-us-reuters-reports">Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li></ul><strong>On Tuesday, a close ally of Flávio Bolsonaro and a US government source confirmed to Reuters that the senator had fled to the US. Flávio failed to meet the deadline set by Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Court to surrender his passports to the Federal Police.</strong></p>

<p>The day before, in a video posted on social media after being summoned by the judiciary, <strong>Flávio </strong><strong>had </strong><strong>denied any intention of leaving Brazil and said he would remain in the country to, as he put it, organize opposition to the government</strong> of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was reelected on Sunday (26) after defeating the senator in the second round of the presidential election.</p>
</description>

    <title>Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/campaign-coordinator-says-he-was-surprised-flavios-escape</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/qRwd5PS8bGdXzP8Jqc3tddJ1J4w=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/lula6539-15.jpg?itok=SWrk3b9E</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/campaign-coordinator-says-he-was-surprised-flavios-escape">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p><strong>Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, told the press on Tuesday (Oct. 27) that he was unaware of Flávio and his family’s departure for the US.</strong><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707039&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707039&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>“We are surprised because yesterday we discussed the need for Flávio - with the 60 million votes he received - to take on a leadership role in the opposition, which is important because, in our assessment, we have a government that has clearly been harmful to the country,” said Marinho after attending a meeting with lawmakers and political leaders from the PL in Brasília.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador">Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaros-party-acknowledges-lulas-victory">Flávio Bolsonaro’s party acknowledges Lula’s victory.</a></li></ul>Marinho also mentioned that he had received a text message from Flávio Bolsonaro around 8 a.m. on Tuesday (27), in which he said he was going to “take some time off” and would later speak with his allies again.</p>

<p><strong>The undisclosed trip to the US, whose details remain unknown, took place less than 48 hours after he lost the presidential election to Lula.</strong> The move was reported by <em>Reuters</em> and confirmed by a US government official.</p>

<p>Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, including Senator-elect Carlos Jordy (PL – Rio de Janeiro), have issued statements confirming his departure.</p>

<p>“Confirmed! Flávio Bolsonaro went to the US to avoid being used as a bargaining chip in efforts to impeach Moraes!” said Jordy, referring to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.</p>

<p>Despite this, no official from Brazil or the US has made a public statement about his departure.</p>

<h2>Investigations</h2>

<p><strong>Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation by the Federal Police in several cases involving alleged crimes such as currency evasion, money laundering, and corruption. </strong>His term as senator for Rio de Janeiro ends in February 2027, when he will lose his special jurisdiction.</p>

<p>Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered on Monday (26) that the former candidate surrender his passports to the police; however, the documents were not handed over.</p>

<p>The court order is part of the case in which Flávio Bolsonaro and attorney Willer Tomaz are being investigated by the Supreme Court for money laundering.</p>

<p>Due to his failure to comply with the order, the Federal Police revoked the senator’s passports.</p>

<p><strong>In a video posted on Monday, Flávio denied that he had plans to leave the country and said he would turn in his passports.</strong></p>

<p><strong><strong>Agência Brasil</strong></strong> contacted Flávio Bolsonaro’s press office but received no response.</p>
</description>

  <item>
    <title>Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador</title>
    <link>https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador</link>
    <imagem-destaque>https://imagens.ebc.com.br/gB-0KZ66r8_sDl3D4YBiwz2kBgw=/1170x700/smart/https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/2026/10/05/2026-10-05t162156z_1_lynxmpem941hc_rtroptp_4_brazil-election.jpg?itok=dL6Sbryj</imagem-destaque>    <description>  <p><p style="text-align:center;"><a class="" href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/internacional/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-crosses-argentine-border-heads-ecuador">
                    <img src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sergiosdlima/assets-ebc@1.0.0/abr/assets/images/logo-agenciabrasil.svg" alt="Logo Agência Brasil" style="height: 54px;">
				</a></p><strong>Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party), his wife, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and their two daughters, Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro, entered Argentina on Tuesday night (Oct. 27).</strong> The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.<img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.png?id=1707022&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /><img src="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/ebc.gif?id=1707022&o=rss" style="width:1px; height:1px; display:inline;" /></p>

<p>In a statement, the agency specified that they crossed the border at 10:50 p.m. via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., according to the Argentine government, Flávio and his family boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly and flew to Guayaquil, Ecuador, as indicated in the flight plan.</p>

<p><h3>Notícias relacionadas:</h3><ul><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/federal-police-revoke-flavio-bolsonaros-passports">Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-rejects-lulas-victory-seeks-annul-election">Flávio Bolsonaro rejects Lula’s victory, seeks to annul election.</a></li><li><a href="https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/politica/noticia/2026-10/flavio-bolsonaro-fled-us-reuters-reports">Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.</a></li></ul>Also, <strong>Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration stated that the four presented valid travel documents and faced no legal impediment to entering the country.</strong> “The crossing was recorded by immigration authorities without incident,” the agency reported.</p>
</description>

entries1.title: Hohe Spritpreise: Bringt der "Tankrabatt" wirklich etwas?
entries1.summary: Seit dem 1. Oktober gilt ein neuer "Tankrabatt". Experten zufolge geben die Mineralölkonzerne die Ersparnis nur zum Teil an die Autofahrer weiter. Der Interessenverband der Branche widerspricht. Von Max Ortmann und Jan Koch.

entries1.title: Kommentar zum "Tankrabatt": Die Regierung schmeißt Milliarden aus dem Fenster
entries1.summary: Vor vier Wochen ist die Neuauflage des "Tankrabatts" in Kraft getreten. Für die Bundesregierung war es eine Beruhigungspille kurz vor den Wahlen, meint Jan Zimmermann. Der Frust an der Tankstelle bleibt jedoch.

entries1.title: Afrika-Gipfel in Russland: Putin umwirbt einen ganzen Kontinent
entries1.summary: Beim Handel mit Afrika liegen China und die EU weit vor Russland. Doch Moskau versucht, seinen Einfluss auf dem Kontinent zu stärken - beim dritten Afrika-Russland-Gipfel waren fast alle afrikanischen Länder dabei. Von Norbert Hahn.

entries1.title: Wie Kanada unter Trumps Zöllen leidet
entries1.summary: Beim heute beginnenden Gipfel in Montreal geht es auch darum, wie eng die Zusammenarbeit mit der EU sein wird. In Kanada sind die Erwartungen groß. Denn die Folgen von Trumps Zöllen sind längst spürbar. Von Giselle Ucar.

entries1.title: Was bringt eine EU-Allianz mit Kanada den Verbrauchern in Europa?
entries1.summary: Die EU und Kanada wollen wirtschaftlich und politisch enger zusammenrücken. Könnte eine verstärkte Kooperation Europas Lieferketten sichern, Preise stabil halten, Abhängigkeiten reduzieren? Von Petra Thiele.

entries1.title: Steinmeier-Rede in China: "Mit Größe und Macht kommt große Verantwortung"
entries1.summary: Bundespräsident Steinmeier hat an der renommierten Peking-Universität eine Rede gehalten. Dabei richtete er klare Forderungen an China - bekundete aber auch seinen Respekt für die Volksrepublik.

entries1.title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Ein Land zwischen Trauer und Aufarbeitung
entries1.summary: Nach dem Zugunglück in Spanien sind Schock und Trauer groß. Forensiker identifizieren weiterhin Todesopfer. Zudem wurden die Gesprächsprotokolle der Leitstelle mit den Lokomotivführern veröffentlicht. Von Julia Macher.

entries1.title: Suche nach Opfern des Zugunglücks in Spanien geht weiter
entries1.summary: In Spanien suchen die Rettungskräfte nach dem schweren Zugunglück nach weiteren Opfern in den Waggon-Trümmern. Die Regierung versprach Aufklärung, in Madrid gab es Proteste. Als Unfallursache könnte menschliches Versagen eine Rolle gespielt haben.

entries1.title: Wer am Samstag auf die Straße geht - und was zu erwarten ist
entries1.summary: Am Samstag soll es in zahlreichen Städten Deutschlands zu Protesten kommen. Nach den Ausschreitungen etwa in Frankreich ist die Sorge vor Gewalt groß. Zu recht? Was sagen die Sicherheitsbehörden, was Experten - und worum geht es eigentlich?

entries1.title: EZB-Chefin Lagarde tritt im Februar vorzeitig zurück
entries1.summary: Gerüchte gab es bereits länger, nun ist es bestätigt: EZB-Chefin Lagarde gibt ihren Posten vorzeitig im Februar auf. So kann über die Nachfolge noch vor der Präsidentschaftswahl in Frankreich entschieden werden.

entries1.title: Europäische Zentralbank hält Leitzins unverändert
entries1.summary: Die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB) hat wie erwartet die Leitzinsen unverändert bei 2,5 Prozent belassen. Für Gesprächsstoff sorgt aber der vorzeitige Rückzug von EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde.

entries1.title: Eralp reagiert auf Spiegel-Bericht
entries1.summary: In nicht für die Öffentlichkeit bestimmten Anmerkungen zu einem Spiegel-Interview sorgte sich Linken-Politikerin Elif Eralp um ihre Sicherheit. Nun bekräftigte sie, klar gegen Gewalt vorgehen zu wollen.

entries1.title: Linken-Politikerin Klein neue Parlamentspräsidentin
entries1.summary: Knapp sechs Wochen nach der Wahl in Berlin ist das Abgeordnetenhaus zu seiner konstituierenden Sitzung zusammengekommen. Die Linken-Politikerin Klein ist zur neuen Präsidentin des Parlaments gewählt worden.

entries1.title: Wie groß ist der politische Einfluss von Stars wie Stevie Wonder?
entries1.summary: Stevie Wonders Musik war immer politisch. Jahrzehntelang war er als Bürgerrechtler aktiv, später machte er Wahlkampf für Obama. Welchen Einfluss haben Popstars - und was machen sie daraus, gerade jetzt, vor den Midterms? Von S. Fritz.

entries1.title: US-Zwischenwahlen: Trump holen seine Versprechen ein
entries1.summary: Er werde das Leben in den USA wieder erschwinglich machen, hatte Trump 2024 versprochen. Zwei Jahre danach sieht die Wirklichkeit anders aus - nicht zuletzt an den Zapfsäulen. Das wirkt sich auf die Umfragen vor den Midterms aus. Von J. Schönenborn.

entries1.title: Zahlreiche Tote bei Angriff auf Bahnhof in Dnipro
entries1.summary: Eine russische Drohne hat nach ukrainischen Angaben am Bahnhof von Dnipro mindestens 14 Menschen getötet. Während Russland und die Ukraine sich weiter gegenseitig mit Drohnen angreifen, hält die Waffenruhe in der Frontstadt Oleschky.

entries1.title: Milliardenverlust bei Volkswagen
entries1.summary: Hohe Abschreibungen und ein schwaches China-Geschäft haben Volkswagen tiefrote Zahlen beschert. Der Konzernverlust lag im dritten Quartal bei 5,8 Milliarden Euro. VW-Aktien fallen.

entries1.title: OVG Lüneburg: AfD darf in Niedersachsen weiter überwacht werden
entries1.summary: Der Verfassungsschutz darf die AfD Niedersachsen vorerst weiter als "gesichert rechtsextremistisch" einstufen und überwachen. Das entschied das Oberverwaltungsgericht Lüneburg. Das Hauptsacheverfahren steht allerdings noch aus.

entries1.title: Möglicher neuer Zwergplanet im Sonnensystem entdeckt
entries1.summary: Am äußeren Rand des Sonnensystems haben Astronomen einen seltenen Himmelskörper entdeckt: einen möglichen neuen Zwergplaneten. Bestätigt sich der Fund, wäre "2026 ED138" erst der sechste bekannte Zwergplanet. Von Uwe Gradwohl.

entries1.title: Opiumproduktion in Afghanistan stark gestiegen
entries1.summary: Die Taliban haben den Anbau von Schlafmohn und die Herstellung von Opium in Afghanistan 2022 verboten. Nun ist die Produktion den UN zufolge erstmals wieder gestiegen - um 400 Prozent innerhalb eines Jahres.

entries1.title: Südafrika bewirbt sich mit der Stadt Durban um Olympia
entries1.summary: Noch nie hat ein afrikanischer Staat Olympische oder Paralympische Spiele ausgerichtet. Südafrika schickt nun Durban für 2036 und 2040 ins Bewerberrennen - einer von derzeit sechs Konkurrenten für München.

entries1.title: Schauspielerin Elke Sommer gestorben
entries1.summary: Sie machte sich in den 1960er-Jahren einen Namen in Hollywood, wurde mit Golden Globe und Bambi ausgezeichnet. Nun ist die deutsche Schauspielerin Elke Sommer im Alter von 85 Jahren gestorben.

entries1.title: Pflegeversicherung: Linnemann schließt Leistungskürzungen nicht aus
entries1.summary: Gesundheitsminister Linnemann hält Einschnitte bei der Pflegeversicherung für möglich. Angesichts steigender Kosten müssten rund zehn Prozent eingespart werden. Patientenschützer warnen vor den Folgen für die häusliche Pflege.

entries1.title: Bayern: Ermittlungen gegen zwei Belarusen wegen Sabotageverdacht
entries1.summary: Zwei Männer aus Belarus stehen im Verdacht, im Raum Nürnberg einen Brandanschlag geplant zu haben - im Auftrag einer fremden Regierung oder Vereinigung. Sie wurden festgenommen und sitzen in Untersuchungshaft. Von Joseph Röhmel.

entries1.title: Rotes Kreuz eröffnet größtes Bevölkerungsschutzzentrum in Brandenburg
entries1.summary: In Brandenburg hat das Deutsche Rote Kreuz ein neues Bevölkerungsschutzzentrum eröffnet. Dort lagert Material, um bei Katastrophen bis zu 5.000 Menschen versorgen zu können. Laut Innenminister Dobrindt setzt das Projekt Maßstäbe.

entries1.title: Kritische Infrastruktur: Mehr Prüfungen auf Sabotagerisiko
entries1.summary: Die Bedrohung für die Kritische Infrastruktur in Deutschland - etwa durch Sabotage oder Spionage - ist gestiegen. Daher will der Bund künftig Beschäftigte in noch mehr Betrieben auf mögliche Sicherheitsrisiken überprüfen.

entries1.title: Weiterhin 14 Monate - Rolle rückwärts beim Elterngeld
entries1.summary: Das Elterngeld bleibt laut Plänen des Familienministeriums bei bis zu 14 Monaten. Eine geplante Kürzung auf zwölf Monate wird nicht umgesetzt. Zudem sollen Mindest- und Höchstbeträge steigen. Von Sarah Beham und Philip Kuntschner.

entries1.title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Der Schock sitzt tief
entries1.summary: In Spanien sitzt der Schock tief über das zweite schwere Zugunglück auf der Hochgeschwindigkeitszugstrecke zwischen Madrid und Andalusien. Mindestens 69 Menschen verloren bei dem Unglück in der Region Toledo ihr Leben. Von Franka Welz.

entries1.title: Brasiliens Wahlverlierer: Bolsonaros spektakuläre Flucht
entries1.summary: Ein Privatflugzeug, Zwischenstopps, die Ankunft in den USA - der brasilianische Wahlverlierer Bolsonaro ist nun in Florida - und bezeichnet sich als "Anführer" Brasiliens. Wie geht das rechte Lager mit dem geflüchteten Bolsonaro um? Von A. Herrberg.

entries1.title: EU-Kanada-Gipfel: Kanada wird vorerst kein "assoziiertes EU-Mitglied"
entries1.summary: Kanzler Merz und andere EU-Regierungschefs haben die Kanada-Pläne von EU-Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen abgeschwächt - kurz vor dem heute beginnenden EU-Kanada-Gipfel. Von einer "assoziierten Mitgliedschaft" ist nicht mehr die Rede. Von S. Fritz.

entries1.title: Hoffnung auf unabhängige Medien in Serbien
entries1.summary: Nach der Niederlage der Vucic-Partei in Serbien hoffen viele Menschen wieder auf eine unabhängige Berichterstattung. Eine Initiative fordert den Entzug der Sendelizenz für Informer - einem Propagandasender im Dienste des Ex-Präsidenten. Von S. Hahne.

entries1.title: Parlamentswahl in Israel: Wofür die arabischen Parteien stehen
entries1.summary: Die arabischen Parteien haben bei der Wahl in Israel wahrscheinlich so stark abgeschnitten wie noch nie. Ihre Unterstützung könnte der Opposition den Weg an die Macht ebnen. Was sind ihre Themen, was sind ihre Ziele? Ein Überblick.

entries1.title: Digitale Barrierefreiheit: Gesetzlich vorgeschrieben, aber oft missachtet
entries1.summary: Die meisten Webseiten verfehlen die gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Mindeststandards der Barrierefreiheit. Das zeigt eine Analyse von BR Data. Die Folge: Menschen mit Behinderung können digitale Angebote oftmals kaum oder gar nicht nutzen. Von Julia Barthel und Marco Lehner.

entries1.title: Junge Menschen im Sog der Sekten
entries1.summary: Junge Menschen fühlen sich von den anhaltenden Krisen besonders belastet. Recherchen des team.recherche vom SWR zeigen, wie Sekten das auszunutzen versuchen. Eine Expertin spricht von "goldenen Zeiten für Sekten".

entries1.title: Deutsche Nachrichtendienste setzen auf Cloud-System von Google
entries1.summary: Um geheime Informationen schneller untereinander austauschen zu können, wollen BND, Verfassungsschutz und MAD ein gemeinsames Cloud-System aufbauen. Nach Recherchen von NDR und WDR soll Google dabei eine maßgebliche Rolle spielen. Von F. Flade und R. Pinkert.

entries1.title: Proteste in Frankreich: KI-generierte Videos und alte Bilder
entries1.summary: Zu den Protesten in Frankreich kursieren viele Bilder und Videos im Netz, die angeblich die Ausschreitungen zeigen. Doch mehrere reichweitenstarke Inhalte sind gefälscht. Von C. Reveland und P. Siggelkow.

entries1.title: Wie Spazierengehen auf die Psyche wirkt
entries1.summary: Gerade jetzt im Herbst kann ein Spaziergang besonders guttun. Studien zeigen, dass regelmäßiges Gehen Stimmung, Gesundheit und soziale Kontakte fördern kann. In einigen Städten haben sich Spazierclubs gebildet. Von Gerald Perschke.

entries1.title: Bericht der Weltwetterorganisation: Immer mehr Treibhausgase in der Atmosphäre
entries1.summary: In der Atmoshäre sammeln sich immer mehr Treibhausgase. Das zeigt ein neuer Bericht der Weltwetterorganisation. Offenbar erholt sich die Natur von Hitze und Trockenheit nicht so schnell wie erwartet. Von N. Gode und S. Biegger.

entries1.title: Quantennetzwerk QuNET: Schutz gegen Hackerangriffe
entries1.summary: Quantencomputer und KI können wohl bald digitale Verschlüsselungen knacken. In Zukunft sollen deshalb Quantennetze wie QuNET die Kommunikation schützen. Die Technologie funktioniert, aber noch nicht perfekt. Von Jan Kerckhoff.

entries1.title: KI-Investitionen tragen nicht überall Früchte
entries1.summary: Die Tech-Giganten im Silicon Valley stecken Milliarden in Künstliche Intelligenz. Doch die investierten Gelder führen nicht automatisch zu Wachstum. Das zeigen die Zahlen von Microsoft und Alphabet.

entries1.title: Merz fordert auf Asienreise neue Allianz für regelbasierten Handel
entries1.summary: Kanzler Merz hat auf bei seinem Japan-Besuch eine Allianz für einen regelkonformen globalen Handel gefordert. Damit könne man besser auf unerlaubte Zölle reagieren. Deutschland ist die drittgrößte Volkswirtschaft der Welt, Japan die viertgrößte.

entries1.title: Wie Meta-Chef Mark Zuckerberg eine Reichensteuer umgehen will
entries1.summary: Kalifornien stimmt bei den Midterms auch über die Einführung einer Reichensteuer ab. In dem US-Bundesstaat leben viele Tech-Milliardäre. Einer von ihnen macht schon mal mobil. Von Gabi Biesinger.

entries1.title: Wo Deutschland noch wachsen kann: Zukunftsmärkte für heimische Firmen
entries1.summary: Die deutsche Wirtschaft hat viele Probleme. Doch bei all den negativen Nachrichten gibt es auch Chancen. Denn auf einigen Märkten der Zukunft haben heimische Unternehmen gute Karten. Von Angela Göpfert.

entries1.title: Mercedes hat noch größere Probleme im chinesischen Markt
entries1.summary: Mercedes hat im dritten Quartal in seiner Autosparte operativ deutlich weniger verdient. Vor allem das schlechte China-Geschäft setzt dem Konzern zu. Die Strategie für den weltgrößten Automarkt will er nun überdenken.

entries1.title: Marktbericht: DAX setzt Klettertour fort
entries1.summary: Die großen Notenbanken halten vorerst die Füße still - die Botschaft hat die Kauflust der Anleger beflügelt, der DAX beendet den Handelstag im Plus. Auch der VW-Schock vom Morgen wurde gut verdaut.

entries1.title: DFB-Pokal: Bayern gegen Magdeburg gnadenlos - auch ohne Kane
entries1.summary: Harry Kane wurde geschont, doch der 1. FC Magdeburg nicht: Bayern München ließ dem mutigen Zweitligisten im DFB-Pokal keine Chance.

entries1.title: DFB-Pokal: Dynamo schießt furchtbar harmlose Schalker ab
entries1.summary: Zweitligist Dynamo Dresden hat sich mit einem verdienten Sieg gegen Bundesligist Schalke 04 für das Achtelfinale im DFB-Pokal qualifiziert.

entries1.title: Ein Nordclub kommt durch - Holstein Kiel im Pokal-Achtelfinale
entries1.summary: Holstein-Torhüter Lio Rothenhagen wurde im Zweitrundenspiel gegen Bundesligist Hoffenheim im Elfmeterschießen zum Kieler Pokalhelden.

entries1.title: Denkmalschutz: Wer sich für unser kulturelles Erbe einsetzt
entries1.summary: Nicht nur der Staat kümmert sich um Denkmalschutz. Auch Privatpersonen und Initiativen engagieren sich für den Erhalt von Kulturgütern. Das ruft Befürworter und Kritiker auf den Plan. Von Susanne Fritz.

entries1.title: Wetter Deutschland: Wolken, Temperaturen, Wind und Aussichten
entries1.summary: Am Freitag herrscht ruhiges Herbstwetter. Dabei ist es im Norden und Osten überwiegend trüb. Sonst scheint neben Nebel- und Hochnebelfeldern gebietsweise auch die Sonne. 7 bis 15 Grad.

entries1.title: Regenradar Deutschland: Aktueller Niederschlag
entries1.summary: Das Regenradar für Deutschland von tagesschau.de: Live-Werte zum Niederschlag und Prognose für die nächsten zwei Stunden.

entries1.title: 11KM-Podcast: AfD-Leak - was die gehackten E-Mails verraten
entries1.summary: Hacker haben Hunderttausende interne E-Mails der AfD veröffentlicht. Journalisten werten das Daten-Leak aus. 11KM mit einem Blick ins Innere der Partei.

entries1.title: Podcast 15 Minuten: Zugunglück in Spanien, Temu-Gebühr, Weinautomat
entries1.summary: Im tagesschau-Podcast 15 Minuten geht es heute um das Zugunglück in Spanien sowie eine neue Gebühr für Päckchen von Temu, Shein und Co. Außerdem: Warum ein Weinautomat für jahrelangen Streit sorgt.

entries2.title: Steinmeier-Rede in China: "Mit Größe und Macht kommt große Verantwortung"
entries2.summary: Bundespräsident Steinmeier hat an der renommierten Peking-Universität eine Rede gehalten. Dabei richtete er klare Forderungen an China - bekundete aber auch seinen Respekt für die Volksrepublik.

entries2.title: Zugunglück in Spanien: Ein Land zwischen Trauer und Aufarbeitung
entries2.summary: Nach dem Zugunglück in Spanien sind Schock und Trauer groß. Forensiker identifizieren weiterhin Todesopfer. Zudem wurden die Gesprächsprotokolle der Leitstelle mit den Lokomotivführern veröffentlicht. Von Julia Macher.

entries2.title: Suche nach Opfern des Zugunglücks in Spanien geht weiter
entries2.summary: In Spanien suchen die Rettungskräfte nach dem schweren Zugunglück nach weiteren Opfern in den Waggon-Trümmern. Die Regierung versprach Aufklärung, in Madrid gab es Proteste. Als Unfallursache könnte menschliches Versagen eine Rolle gespielt haben.

entries2.title: Wer am Samstag auf die Straße geht - und was zu erwarten ist
entries2.summary: Am Samstag soll es in zahlreichen Städten Deutschlands zu Protesten kommen. Nach den Ausschreitungen etwa in Frankreich ist die Sorge vor Gewalt groß. Zu recht? Was sagen die Sicherheitsbehörden, was Experten - und worum geht es eigentlich?

entries2.title: EZB-Chefin Lagarde tritt im Februar vorzeitig zurück
entries2.summary: Gerüchte gab es bereits länger, nun ist es bestätigt: EZB-Chefin Lagarde gibt ihren Posten vorzeitig im Februar auf. So kann über die Nachfolge noch vor der Präsidentschaftswahl in Frankreich entschieden werden.

entries2.title: Europäische Zentralbank hält Leitzins unverändert
entries2.summary: Die Europäische Zentralbank (EZB) hat wie erwartet die Leitzinsen unverändert bei 2,5 Prozent belassen. Für Gesprächsstoff sorgt aber der vorzeitige Rückzug von EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde.

entries2.title: Eralp reagiert auf Spiegel-Bericht
entries2.summary: In nicht für die Öffentlichkeit bestimmten Anmerkungen zu einem Spiegel-Interview sorgte sich Linken-Politikerin Elif Eralp um ihre Sicherheit. Nun bekräftigte sie, klar gegen Gewalt vorgehen zu wollen.

entries2.title: Linken-Politikerin Klein neue Parlamentspräsidentin
entries2.summary: Knapp sechs Wochen nach der Wahl in Berlin ist das Abgeordnetenhaus zu seiner konstituierenden Sitzung zusammengekommen. Die Linken-Politikerin Klein ist zur neuen Präsidentin des Parlaments gewählt worden.

entries2.title: Wie groß ist der politische Einfluss von Stars wie Stevie Wonder?
entries2.summary: Stevie Wonders Musik war immer politisch. Jahrzehntelang war er als Bürgerrechtler aktiv, später machte er Wahlkampf für Obama. Welchen Einfluss haben Popstars - und was machen sie daraus, gerade jetzt, vor den Midterms? Von S. Fritz.

entries2.title: US-Zwischenwahlen: Trump holen seine Versprechen ein
entries2.summary: Er werde das Leben in den USA wieder erschwinglich machen, hatte Trump 2024 versprochen. Zwei Jahre danach sieht die Wirklichkeit anders aus - nicht zuletzt an den Zapfsäulen. Das wirkt sich auf die Umfragen vor den Midterms aus. Von J. Schönenborn.

entries2.title: Zahlreiche Tote bei Angriff auf Bahnhof in Dnipro
entries2.summary: Eine russische Drohne hat nach ukrainischen Angaben am Bahnhof von Dnipro mindestens 14 Menschen getötet. Während Russland und die Ukraine sich weiter gegenseitig mit Drohnen angreifen, hält die Waffenruhe in der Frontstadt Oleschky.

entries2.title: Milliardenverlust bei Volkswagen
entries2.summary: Hohe Abschreibungen und ein schwaches China-Geschäft haben Volkswagen tiefrote Zahlen beschert. Der Konzernverlust lag im dritten Quartal bei 5,8 Milliarden Euro. VW-Aktien fallen.

entries2.title: OVG Lüneburg: AfD darf in Niedersachsen weiter überwacht werden
entries2.summary: Der Verfassungsschutz darf die AfD Niedersachsen vorerst weiter als "gesichert rechtsextremistisch" einstufen und überwachen. Das entschied das Oberverwaltungsgericht Lüneburg. Das Hauptsacheverfahren steht allerdings noch aus.

entries2.title: Möglicher neuer Zwergplanet im Sonnensystem entdeckt
entries2.summary: Am äußeren Rand des Sonnensystems haben Astronomen einen seltenen Himmelskörper entdeckt: einen möglichen neuen Zwergplaneten. Bestätigt sich der Fund, wäre "2026 ED138" erst der sechste bekannte Zwergplanet. Von Uwe Gradwohl.

entries2.title: Opiumproduktion in Afghanistan stark gestiegen
entries2.summary: Die Taliban haben den Anbau von Schlafmohn und die Herstellung von Opium in Afghanistan 2022 verboten. Nun ist die Produktion den UN zufolge erstmals wieder gestiegen - um 400 Prozent innerhalb eines Jahres.

entries2.title: Südafrika bewirbt sich mit der Stadt Durban um Olympia
entries2.summary: Noch nie hat ein afrikanischer Staat Olympische oder Paralympische Spiele ausgerichtet. Südafrika schickt nun Durban für 2036 und 2040 ins Bewerberrennen - einer von derzeit sechs Konkurrenten für München.

entries2.title: Schauspielerin Elke Sommer gestorben
entries2.summary: Sie machte sich in den 1960er-Jahren einen Namen in Hollywood, wurde mit Golden Globe und Bambi ausgezeichnet. Nun ist die deutsche Schauspielerin Elke Sommer im Alter von 85 Jahren gestorben.
